nodes.title: ICU Admission
nodes.summary: ICU for severe NMS. Modern mortality ~5-10% in-hospital (30-day ~4.7%), historically up to 20%.
nodes.body: ICU mandatory for: [1][2][6] * Temp >40 degC * Severe rigidity * Rhabdomyolysis (CK >10,000) * Respiratory compromise * Renal failure * Autonomic instability Mortality: Historically reported at 10-20%, but contemporary cohorts are lower — ~5-10% in-hospital, with 30-day mortality near 4.7% and 1-year mortality ~15.1% in recent data. Risk rises with delayed diagnosis, severe rhabdomyolysis, and ren
nodes.recommendation: ICU admission for severe NMS.

nodes.title: Step-down Admission
nodes.summary: Step-down for moderate. Average stay 7-14 days.
nodes.body: Step-down/telemetry for: [1][2][8] * Mild-moderate symptoms * Stable vitals * CK <10,000 * No respiratory compromise Continue: * Bromocriptine * Benzos PRN * Aggressive hydration * Serial CK and renal function Duration: Average hospitalization 7-14 days. [4][8]
nodes.recommendation: Step-down admission for moderate NMS.

nodes.title: The Generally Unwell Elder — Sick Check First
nodes.summary: Atypical is normal in elders. Full vitals incl glucose/temp/orthostatics + ECG + mental status vs baseline. Resuscitate in parallel if unstable.
nodes.body: \u26A0\uFE0F "Weak / off / not right" in an elder is high-risk. Do NOT accept a vague label without a source hunt. Atypical presentation is the rule after ~75: sepsis without fever, MI without chest pain, "acute abdomen" with a soft belly, stroke as "confusion." How high-risk, in numbers (Basel BANC cohort, ED patients presenting with nonspecific complaints): a serious condition \u2014 life-threat

nodes.title: Rule In / Rule Out — Systematic Source Hunt
nodes.summary: Structured multi-system source hunt; work each to a verdict. Excluded loops back. Anchoring is the enemy.
nodes.body: The vague elder needs a broad, structured hunt \u2014 work each system to an explicit verdict. Excluded loops back here for the next branch. Cast a wide net early; anchoring is the enemy. Related hubs \u2014 use the one that matches the dominant finding: if the leading problem is a change in mental status, work Altered Mental Status Hub. If it is true motor weakness rather than global "off," work

nodes.title: Occult Sepsis — Source & Physiology Gate
nodes.summary: Elders septic atypically (delirium/falls/anorexia). Hunt all sources; qSOFA prompts. Do not anchor on asymptomatic bacteriuria.
nodes.body: Elders septic without classic signs: delirium, functional decline, falls, or anorexia may be the ONLY presentation. Fever can be absent (or hypothermia present). Hunt every source: urine (but do NOT anchor on asymptomatic bacteriuria), lungs, skin/soft tissue, intra-abdominal, CNS, lines/devices. Use qSOFA (RR\u226522, SBP\u2264100, altered) as a bedside prompt \u2014 a low qSOFA does NOT exclude

nodes.title: Sepsis / Serious Infection — Treat
nodes.body: Open Sepsis. Route to the source consult as it declares: Adult UTI \u00B7 Pneumonia \u00B7 Meningitis. Next hour (source-directed): - Cultures before antibiotics (blood \u00D7 2, urine, sputum, CSF if CNS concern) \u2014 do not delay antibiotics for LP in a toxic patient. - Broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 h, narrowed to the suspected source and local antibiogram. - Balanced-crystalloid resusci
nodes.recommendation: Cultures then broad-spectrum abx within 1 h; measured crystalloid with cardiopulmonary reassessment; source control. Never anchor on asymptomatic bacteriuria.

nodes.title: Sepsis — Unlikely (Beware Bacteriuria Anchoring)
nodes.body: No sepsis physiology and no convincing source make serious infection less likely now. The classic geriatric error is stopping at a positive urinalysis \u2014 asymptomatic bacteriuria is common in elders and treating it does not explain a vague decline. Keep the source hunt open. Re-image / reassess if delirium worsens, temperature trends, or lactate rises. Return to the hub for the next branch.
nodes.recommendation: Sepsis unlikely now; do NOT treat asymptomatic bacteriuria as the cause; keep hunting and reassess if delirium/temp/lactate worsen.

nodes.title: Silent / Atypical Cardiac — ECG Gate
nodes.summary: ECG + troponin on every unwell elder. 33% of all MIs are painless; ~60% in those over 85. Also screen arrhythmia + decompensated HF.
nodes.body: Painless MI is not a rarity in this population, and the usual "about a third" figure understates the risk in the oldest patients. In the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction (434,877 confirmed MIs), 33% presented without chest pain overall \u2014 but the proportion is steeply age-dependent: in patients over 85, only ~40% report chest pain at all, meaning roughly 60% of MIs in the very old ar

nodes.title: Cardiac Cause — Treat
nodes.body: ACS: open STEMI or NSTEMI. Aspirin, ECG-driven pathway, serial troponin; use HEART/GRACE to risk-stratify NSTE presentations. Unstable arrhythmia (rapid AF with instability, high-grade AV block): rate/rhythm control or pacing per ACLS. Decompensated heart failure: treat congestion (diuresis, NIV for pulmonary edema) and hunt the trigger (ischemia, arrhythmia, infection, non-adherence). Admit for m
nodes.recommendation: ACS \u2192 ASA + ECG pathway + serial troponin; unstable arrhythmia \u2192 ACLS; decompensated HF \u2192 treat congestion + find trigger.

nodes.title: Cardiac Cause — Unlikely
nodes.body: A non-ischemic ECG with a flat troponin and no arrhythmia or heart-failure signs makes an acute cardiac cause less likely. In elders, use serial troponin + repeat ECG if the story is at all concerning \u2014 a single set does not clear silent ischemia. Return to the hub for the next branch.
nodes.recommendation: Cardiac cause unlikely now; serial troponin + repeat ECG if the presentation stays concerning.

nodes.title: Neurologic — Stroke vs Delirium Gate
nodes.summary: Glucose first. Focal deficit = stroke pathway; fluctuating global confusion = delirium workup; no change = move on.
nodes.body: Check a glucose first (hypoglycemia mimics stroke). Then distinguish an acute focal deficit (stroke \u2014 time-critical) from delirium (acute, fluctuating global inattention off baseline). A posterior stroke can present as isolated vertigo, ataxia, or "confusion" without obvious weakness \u2014 examine gait, eye movements, and coordination.

nodes.title: Acute Stroke Syndrome — Treat
nodes.body: Open Stroke. Next minutes: confirm glucose, establish last-known-well, NIHSS, emergent non-contrast head CT \u00B1 CTA/perfusion, activate stroke pathway for thrombolysis / thrombectomy eligibility. Do not let "the patient is just confused" delay the clock \u2014 posterior and "confusion-predominant" strokes are missed this way.
nodes.recommendation: Glucose + last-known-well + NIHSS + emergent CT/CTA; activate stroke pathway. Beware confusion-predominant/posterior strokes.

nodes.title: Delirium — Find the Cause
nodes.body: Open Delirium. Delirium is a symptom, not a diagnosis \u2014 it demands a cause hunt (infection, drugs, metabolic, hypoxia, pain, urinary retention/constipation, stroke, cardiac). Prevalence and detection \u2014 the numbers you should hold: pooled prevalence of delirium in older ED patients is 15.2% (95% CI 12.5\u201318.0%) across 30 studies and 19,534 patients \u2014 not the 20\u201330% often quo
nodes.recommendation: Screen with a validated tool (4AT/bCAM/CAM-ICU/mCAM-ED/AMT-4/RASS; DTS to rule out only). Delirium = cause hunt (infection/drugs/metabolic/hypoxia/retention/stroke). Non-pharm first; avoid benzodiazepines.

nodes.title: Acute Neurologic Cause — Unlikely
nodes.body: No acute focal deficit and no change from cognitive baseline make an acute neurologic cause less likely. Confirm baseline with a collateral history \u2014 families often normalize slow decline. If there is any doubt about acuity, image and reassess. Return to the hub for the next branch.
nodes.recommendation: Acute neuro cause unlikely; confirm baseline via collateral history; image if acuity is uncertain.

nodes.title: Metabolic / Endocrine — Panel Gate
nodes.summary: Broad panel: glucose, Na, Ca, K, renal, TSH, cortisol. Correct derangements carefully (esp. Na rate).
nodes.body: Send a broad panel: glucose, sodium, calcium, potassium, renal function, TSH, and (if suggestive) cortisol. Hyponatremia, hyper/hypoglycemia, hypercalcemia, uremia, thyroid storm/myxedema, and adrenal crisis all present as nonspecific decline in elders.

nodes.title: Metabolic / Endocrine Crisis — Treat
nodes.body: - Hypoglycemia: open Hypoglycemia \u2014 treat immediately (D50 / glucagon), then find the cause (sulfonylurea, insulin, sepsis, renal, adrenal); admit sulfonylurea/long-acting insulin events for recurrence. - Hyperglycemic crisis: open DKA (or HHS pathway) \u2014 fluids, electrolytes (K+ before insulin), insulin, treat trigger. - Adrenal crisis: open Adrenal Insufficiency \u2014 hydrocortisone 10
nodes.recommendation: Correct the derangement by acuity: hypoglycemia now; adrenal crisis \u2192 hydrocortisone empirically; hyponatremia \u2264 8 mEq/L/24 h; treat the underlying cause.

nodes.title: Metabolic Cause — Unlikely
nodes.body: A normal broad metabolic/endocrine panel makes a metabolic crisis unlikely as the driver. Recheck if the clinical picture evolves or if a targeted test (e.g., random cortisol, ionized calcium) was not yet sent. Return to the hub for the next branch.
nodes.recommendation: Metabolic cause unlikely on a normal panel; send targeted tests (cortisol, ionized Ca) if suggested and reassess.

nodes.title: Occult Trauma / Environmental — Gate
nodes.summary: Found-down elder = trauma. Anticoagulated + head strike = CT head; can\u2019t bear weight = fracture imaging; temp derangement = environmental.
nodes.body: Ask about unwitnessed falls (a "found down" elder is trauma until proven otherwise). On anticoagulation, an intracranial bleed can present as isolated confusion. Screen for hip/pelvic fracture (pain, inability to bear weight, leg shortening/rotation) and temperature extremes (hypothermia can look like sepsis or stroke; hyperthermia/heat illness in summer).

nodes.title: Suspected Intracranial Injury — Image
nodes.body: Non-contrast head CT now for any anticoagulated / antiplatelet elder with a fall or head strike, or any focal deficit / decreased GCS. \u2014 delayed bleeds occur; consider a period of observation \u00B1 repeat CT for anticoagulated patients even with an initially normal scan. If bleed: reverse anticoagulation emergently (per agent \u2014 e.g., 4-factor PCC + vitamin K for warfarin, andexanet/PCC
nodes.recommendation: Non-contrast head CT for anticoagulated fall / focal deficit; reverse anticoagulation emergently if bleed + neurosurgery; delayed ICH ~1.8-2.6% so target repeat imaging/observation selectively rather than universally.

nodes.title: Suspected Fracture — Image
nodes.body: Inability to bear weight, hip/groin pain, or leg shortening/external rotation after a fall \u2192 plain films; if negative but clinical suspicion persists, MRI (or CT) for occult hip fracture. Pelvic fractures in elders can bleed significantly \u2014 open Pelvic Fracture if pelvic mechanism / instability. Analgesia (fascia-iliaca block is excellent for hip fractures), orthopedics, and admission.
nodes.recommendation: Plain films \u2192 MRI/CT for occult hip fracture; pelvic fracture pathway if pelvic mechanism; regional analgesia + orthopedics.

nodes.title: Environmental Temperature Illness — Treat
nodes.body: - Hypothermia (core <35\u00B0C): open Hypothermia \u2014 handle gently (arrhythmia risk), active rewarming by severity, and hunt a precipitant (sepsis, hypothyroid, hypoglycemia, intoxication, occult fall). - Heat illness / hyperthermia: open Heat Stroke \u2014 rapid cooling, organ-support; elders on anticholinergics/diuretics are high-risk. Temperature derangement in an elder is often a clue to a
nodes.recommendation: Rewarm/cool by severity AND hunt the precipitant; temperature derangement is a clue, not the full diagnosis.

nodes.title: Occult Trauma / Environmental — Unlikely
nodes.body: No trauma history and a normal temperature make occult injury / environmental illness less likely. Collateral history matters \u2014 an elder may not recall or report a fall. If bruising, anticoagulation, or an unclear timeline raises concern, image the head. Return to the hub for the next branch.
nodes.recommendation: Occult trauma unlikely; confirm with collateral history; image head if anticoagulated with any concern.

nodes.title: Medication / Polypharmacy — Review Gate
nodes.summary: Full med reconciliation. Age 65+ = 34.5% of ADE ED visits; anticoagulants + diabetes agents + opioids = 59.9%. Beers "avoid" drugs only 1.8%.
nodes.body: Reconcile every medication. In elders, an adverse drug event is a leading cause of nonspecific decline: new drug started, dose change, interaction, or accumulation with worsening renal function. High-yield culprits: anticoagulants (bleeding), sedatives/opioids/anticholinergics (delirium, falls), diuretics/ACEi (electrolytes, AKI), sulfonylureas/insulin (hypoglycemia), digoxin/lithium (toxicity), a

nodes.title: Adverse Drug Event — Address
nodes.body: - Stop or hold the offending agent; check drug levels where relevant (digoxin, lithium, valproate, phenytoin). - Specific management: digoxin toxicity \u2192 Digibind for life-threatening features; serotonin syndrome \u2192 stop serotonergics + supportive \u00B1 cyproheptadine; anticholinergic toxicity \u2192 supportive; benzodiazepine/opioid excess \u2192 support airway (flumazenil generally avoi
nodes.recommendation: Hold the culprit, check levels, give the specific antidote where indicated, correct downstream effects, deprescribe + communicate.

nodes.title: Medication Cause — Unlikely
nodes.body: A careful reconciliation without a plausible culprit makes an adverse drug event less likely. Recheck adherence and OTC/supplement use (elders under-report these), and re-screen if renal function changes make a previously safe dose toxic. Return to the hub for the next branch.
nodes.recommendation: Drug cause unlikely on reconciliation; recheck OTC/supplement use + adherence + renal-dose accumulation.

nodes.title: Initial Bundle — Broad Screen for the Vague Elder
nodes.summary: Broad screen: ECG + glucose + temp + orthostatics; CBC/CMP/troponin/lactate/VBG/UA + targeted tests; collateral history. Reassess on results.
nodes.body: No single life-threat ruled in yet. Because the miss rate is high, the vague elder earns a broad initial screen rather than a narrow one: - Bedside now: ECG, POC glucose, temperature, SpO2, orthostatic vitals if feasible. - Labs: CBC with differential, CMP (Na, Ca, renal, glucose), troponin, lactate, VBG, urinalysis + culture (interpret cautiously), and per story: TSH, cortisol, LFTs, ammonia, dru

nodes.title: Reassess — Results & Second Look
nodes.summary: Source declared = route out; undifferentiated + safe = discharge w/ follow-up; not at baseline = admit; deteriorating = STOP.
nodes.body: Integrate results, collateral history, and a repeat exam. Decide the next step.

nodes.title: Imaging & Workup Breadth
nodes.summary: Image by leading hypothesis with a lower threshold than in the young: head CT (fall/delirium), CXR, CT A/P for occult source, POCUS for volume/retention.
nodes.body: Image by the leading hypothesis \u2014 but the vague elder often justifies broader imaging than a younger patient with the same complaint: - Non-contrast head CT: any focal deficit, decreased GCS, fall/anticoagulation, or unexplained delirium. - CXR: occult pneumonia, heart failure, effusion. - CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast: unexplained sepsis source, abdominal tenderness, suspected obstruction/

nodes.title: Disposition
nodes.summary: Admit if diagnosis found / unsafe / high-risk undifferentiated; discharge only if back to baseline + safe home + follow-up. Document CFS; never disposition on the score alone.
nodes.body: Disposition in the vague elder is as much about safety and function as about a single diagnosis. Weigh baseline, supports, and reversibility. Document frailty explicitly \u2014 it is the variable that predicts what happens after you decide. The Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS, 1\u20139) is the instrument the Geriatric ED Guidelines framework uses; scores in the vulnerable-to-frail range (CFS \u22654)

nodes.title: Admit / Observe
nodes.body: Admit (or place in observation) when: a serious diagnosis is found or strongly suspected, the patient is not back to functional baseline, cannot safely self-care / lacks supports, has an abnormal vital sign or lab trend, is on high-risk medications with an unresolved concern, or has an unexplained decline that is not yet safe to send home. Do NOT discharge a "weak/off" elder purely because the tes
nodes.recommendation: Admit for a found or high-risk undifferentiated cause OR any elder not at functional baseline; don\u2019t discharge on "normal labs" alone; screen for abuse; carry baseline + goals in handoff.

nodes.title: Discharge — Only With a Tight Safety Net
nodes.body: Discharge is reasonable ONLY when: a plausible benign/reversible cause was addressed (or a broad screen is reassuring), the patient is back to functional baseline, can safely eat/drink/toilet/ambulate to baseline, has capable supports, and has reliable, prompt follow-up. Before discharge: (1) confirm baseline with collateral, (2) reconcile medications + deprescribe culprits, (3) ensure gait/fall s
nodes.recommendation: Discharge only if back to baseline + safe supports + booked 48-72 h follow-up; reconcile meds, ensure fall safety, large-print precautions, involve family.

nodes.title: NSTEMI Confirmed
nodes.summary: Aspirin 162-325mg chewed, NTG 0.4mg SL (rule out RV infarct first), ECG in 10min, serial troponins — morphine only if refractory
nodes.body: Establish diagnosis: troponin rise AND at least one of ischemic symptoms, new ST depression/T-wave inversion, or wall motion abnormality. Immediate actions: \u2022 Aspirin 162\u2013325 mg chewed \u2022 Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL q5min \u00D7 3 \u2014 rule out RV infarction first \u2022 Morphine ONLY for refractory pain (may increase mortality) \u2022 Supplemental O\u2082 only if SpO\u2082 <90% \u2022

nodes.title: Anticoagulation Selection
nodes.summary: Choose ONE anticoagulant — enoxaparin preferred, UFH if CrCl<30 or PCI within 24h, fondaparinux lowest bleed risk; do NOT switch agents
nodes.body: Choose ONE anticoagulation strategy: \u2022 Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC q12h \u2014 preferred for most patients \u2022 UFH 60 units/kg bolus (max 4,000), 12 units/kg/hr (max 1,000) \u2014 preferred if CrCl <30 or PCI within 24h \u2022 Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC daily \u2014 preferred for conservative strategy (lowest bleeding risk per OASIS-5) Do NOT switch between anticoagulants (increases bleeding risk).

nodes.title: Immediate Risk Assessment
nodes.summary: Screen for emergent cath (<2h): cardiogenic shock, refractory pain, sustained VT/VF, acute MR/VSD, new pulmonary edema
nodes.body: Assess for features requiring emergent catheterization (<2 hours): \u2022 Hemodynamic instability (cardiogenic shock) \u2022 Refractory/recurrent chest pain despite medical therapy \u2022 Sustained ventricular arrhythmias (VT/VF) \u2022 Acute mitral regurgitation or VSD \u2022 Signs of heart failure (new pulmonary edema)

nodes.title: Emergent Catheterization (<2 hours)
nodes.body: Immediate PCI indicated. \u2022 Activate cath lab \u2022 UFH preferred anticoagulation (can titrate in cath lab) \u2022 If on fondaparinux: supplement with UFH 60 units/kg IV bolus (catheter thrombosis risk) \u2022 P2Y12 inhibitor loading: Ticagrelor 180 mg OR Prasugrel 60 mg (if no prior stroke/TIA) \u2022 Consider Metoprolol if HR >100 and no contraindications \u2022 Bedside Echo (POCUS) for wal
nodes.recommendation: Emergent PCI. Activate cath lab immediately. UFH preferred. Load P2Y12 inhibitor.

nodes.title: TIMI Risk Score Stratification
nodes.summary: TIMI score guides timing: 0-2 conservative, 3 delayed invasive (25-72h), 4-7 early invasive (<24h)
nodes.body: Use the TIMI Risk Score to guide invasive strategy timing.

nodes.title: Conservative (Ischemia-Guided) Strategy
nodes.summary: Low TIMI: fondaparinux preferred (lowest bleed), metoprolol, atorvastatin 80mg, clopidogrel 300mg load, stress test before discharge
nodes.body: Low TIMI risk. Conservative management appropriate. See Conservative Management Details Medical therapy: \u2022 Continue anticoagulation (fondaparinux preferred \u2014 lowest bleeding) \u2022 Metoprolol \u2014 target HR <70 \u2022 Nitroglycerin PRN chest pain \u2022 Atorvastatin 80 mg PO (start immediately) \u2022 Clopidogrel 300 mg loading if no P2Y12 yet (ticagrelor also acceptable) Stress test

nodes.title: Early Invasive Strategy (<24 hours)
nodes.summary: TIMI ≥4: cath within 24h, ticagrelor 180mg preferred (PLATO NNT 54), continue anticoag without switching, atorvastatin 80mg
nodes.body: TIMI \u22654 (high risk). Cardiac catheterization within 24 hours. Pre-PCI preparation: \u2022 P2Y12 loading: Ticagrelor 180 mg preferred (PLATO: NNT 54 for CV death/MI/stroke) \u2022 Alternative: Clopidogrel 600 mg if ticagrelor not available or on OAC \u2022 Continue anticoagulation (do NOT switch agents) \u2022 NPO (anticipate catheterization) \u2022 Metoprolol \u2014 target HR <70 if tolerated

nodes.title: Delayed Invasive Strategy (25\u201372 hours)
nodes.summary: TIMI 3 or failed conservative: cath 25-72h, P2Y12 loading, may defer P2Y12 until anatomy known, continue beta-blocker/statin/anticoag
nodes.body: TIMI 3 (intermediate risk) or failed conservative strategy. Cardiac catheterization within 25\u201372 hours. \u2022 Allows stabilization with medical therapy \u2022 Same pre-PCI preparation as early invasive \u2022 P2Y12 loading: Ticagrelor 180 mg OR Clopidogrel 300\u2013600 mg \u2022 If deferring P2Y12 until anatomy known: acceptable strategy per guidelines \u2022 Continue beta-blocker, statin, a

nodes.title: Post-PCI P2Y12 Selection
nodes.summary: P2Y12 for 12mo DAPT: ticagrelor preferred (aspirin ≤100mg), prasugrel if high ischemic risk (CI if prior stroke), clopidogrel if on OAC
nodes.body: Select P2Y12 inhibitor for 12-month DAPT. See P2Y12 Selection Guide Preferred: Ticagrelor 90 mg BID \u2022 PLATO trial: reduced CV death/MI/stroke vs clopidogrel (NNT 54) \u2022 Aspirin \u2264100 mg/day required High ischemic risk (diabetes, stent thrombosis): Prasugrel 10 mg daily \u2022 TRITON-TIMI 38: more potent, but more bleeding \u2022 CONTRAINDICATED if prior stroke/TIA \u2022 Avoid if age

nodes.title: CABG Indicated
nodes.body: Coronary anatomy indicates CABG (e.g., left main, multivessel disease with diabetes). P2Y12 hold times before surgery: \u2022 Ticagrelor: hold \u22653 days (minimum), ideally 5 days \u2022 Clopidogrel: hold \u22655 days \u2022 Prasugrel: hold \u22657 days Continue aspirin. Restart P2Y12 inhibitor 24\u201348h post-CABG. Refer cardiac surgery.
nodes.recommendation: CABG referral. Hold P2Y12 per timing guidelines. Continue aspirin. Restart P2Y12 24\u201348h post-operatively.

nodes.title: DAPT Duration & Special Populations
nodes.summary: Standard 12mo DAPT; NEW 2025 Class 1: 1mo DAPT → ticagrelor monotherapy if high bleed risk (ULTIMATE-DAPT/T-PASS); extend beyond 12mo if high ischemic risk (PEGASUS)
nodes.body: Standard DAPT: 12 months post-PCI (Class 1, 2025 ACC/AHA ACS) \u2022 Aspirin 81 mg + P2Y12 inhibitor daily High bleeding risk \u2014 NEW Class 1 (2025 ACC/AHA): \u2022 DAPT \u00D7 1 month, then ticagrelor monotherapy (ULTIMATE-DAPT, T-PASS) \u2022 BARC 2\u20135 bleeding halved without increase in MACCE Other de-escalation options after 1\u20133 months if high bleeding risk: \u2022 Switch from tica

nodes.title: MINOCA \u2014 Non-Obstructive Coronaries
nodes.body: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (\u226450% stenosis on angiography). Present in 5\u201310% of MI patients. See MINOCA Workup & Management Etiologies: \u2022 Coronary spasm (most common) \u2022 Plaque disruption/erosion \u2022 Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) \u2022 Takotsubo cardiomyopathy \u2022 Myocarditis KEY: Standard ACS regimens may be HARMFUL depend
nodes.recommendation: Individualized therapy based on etiology. Cardiac MRI mandatory. Standard ACS regimen may be harmful \u2014 determine etiology first.

nodes.title: Discharge Medications
nodes.summary: Five pillars post-ACS: DAPT, high-intensity statin, beta-blocker, ACEi/ARB, aldosterone antagonist if EF≤40%; PPI with DAPT (not omeprazole)
nodes.body: The 5 pillars of post-ACS pharmacotherapy: 1. DAPT: Aspirin 81 mg + P2Y12 inhibitor \u00D7 12 months 2. Statin: Atorvastatin 80 mg (or rosuvastatin 20\u201340 mg) \u2014 target LDL <70 3. Beta-blocker: Metoprolol succinate \u2014 continue if EF <40% or hypertension; may discontinue after 1 year if EF preserved 4. ACE inhibitor/ARB: Start within 24h if EF \u226440%, hypertension, or diabetes. Consi

nodes.title: Risk Factor Modification
nodes.summary: Target BP<130/80, LDL<70, HbA1c<7%, smoking cessation (NNT 12); cardiac rehab 36 sessions = 25% CV mortality reduction
nodes.body: Targets: \u2022 BP <130/80 mmHg \u2022 LDL <70 mg/dL (consider <55 if very high risk) \u2022 HbA1c <7% (individualized) \u2022 BMI <25 (or waist <102 cm M, <88 cm F) \u2022 Smoking cessation \u2014 NNT 12 for mortality reduction Cardiac rehabilitation: \u2022 Class I recommendation (36 sessions over 12 weeks) \u2022 25% relative reduction in cardiovascular mortality \u2022 Improves functional capa

nodes.title: Triple Therapy \u2014 AF + ACS + Stent
nodes.body: Patient requires both anticoagulation (AF) and DAPT (stent). Triple therapy (OAC + aspirin + P2Y12) for SHORTEST possible duration: \u2022 1 week (if high bleeding risk) to 1 month maximum \u2022 Then dual therapy: OAC + Clopidogrel 75 mg daily (preferred P2Y12 for triple/dual) \u2022 At 12 months: OAC alone (discontinue P2Y12) Preferred DOAC: Rivaroxaban 15 mg daily (PIONEER AF-PCI) or Apixaban 5
nodes.recommendation: Minimize triple therapy duration (\u22641 month). DOAC + clopidogrel preferred for dual therapy phase. Discontinue antiplatelet at 12 months.

nodes.title: Post-MI Heart Failure Management
nodes.body: EF \u226440% post-MI = high-risk. Initiate guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT): Core GDMT (start before discharge): \u2022 ACE inhibitor or ARB (or ARNI if stable) \u2014 SAVE, VALIANT trials \u2022 Beta-blocker (Metoprolol succinate or carvedilol) \u2014 CAPRICORN trial \u2022 Aldosterone antagonist (eplerenone 25\u201350 mg or spironolactone) if EF \u226440% + HF symptoms or diabetes \u201
nodes.recommendation: Initiate 4-pillar GDMT before discharge. Reassess EF at 3 months. Evaluate for ICD if EF \u226435% after 40 days.

nodes.title: Follow-Up Plan
nodes.body: Post-discharge follow-up: \u2022 Cardiology: 1\u20132 weeks \u2022 PCP: 2\u20134 weeks \u2022 Cardiac rehab: referral before discharge (36 sessions) \u2022 Stress test at 4\u20136 weeks if not revascularized \u2022 Echo at 3 months if EF <50% at presentation \u2022 Lab work: lipid panel at 4\u201312 weeks (LDL target <70) DAPT adherence counseling: \u2022 Do NOT stop P2Y12 without cardiology guida
nodes.recommendation: Cardiology follow-up in 1\u20132 weeks. Cardiac rehab referral. Emphasize DAPT adherence. LDL target <70 mg/dL.

nodes.title: Greater Occipital Nerve Block — ED Procedure
nodes.summary: Peripheral block: 5-15 min onset, 4-6 h LA duration, ~78% acute cluster response.
nodes.body: Bedside peripheral block for cluster headache rescue, occipital neuralgia, cervicogenic headache, post-traumatic headache, hemicrania continua, and refractory status migrainosus. Open first: - Procedure Steps Summary - Anatomy Reference - Stop / Pitfalls Return to Headache Hub for the broader workup if diagnosis is uncertain.

nodes.title: Why Are You Blocking?
nodes.summary: Cluster (acute + bridge), occipital neuralgia, cervicogenic, post-traumatic, refractory status migrainosus.
nodes.body: Confirm a benign headache phenotype has been worked up. Secondary causes (SAH, dissection, CVST, AACG, hypertensive emergency, meningitis) MUST be excluded first.

nodes.title: Return to Headache Hub for Workup
nodes.body: No clear indication for occipital block. Re-screen for red flags + complete diagnostic workup before considering a procedural option. Open Headache Hub.
nodes.recommendation: Do not perform ONB without a defined indication.

nodes.title: Contraindications + Pre-procedure Checks
nodes.summary: No skin infection, no LA allergy, document anticoag risk/benefit; no steroid in pregnancy.
nodes.body: Absolute: - Overlying skin infection at injection site - Known allergy to local anesthetic class (amide LA cross-reactivity is rare; ester allergy is more common) - Patient refusal Relative — escalate / consult: - Therapeutic anticoagulation (INR >3, new DOAC dose <24 h, unfractionated heparin gtt) — per ASRA 2018 deep peripheral block guidance, ONB is superficial and bleeding risk is low, but doc

nodes.title: Anatomy — GON, LON, Occipital Artery
nodes.summary: GON medial to occipital artery, 1/3 inion-mastoid; LON lateral, 2/3 distance.
nodes.body: Greater Occipital Nerve (GON): - Origin: medial branch of C2 dorsal ramus - Emerges through trapezius/semispinalis capitis ~2-3 cm lateral to midline at the level of the superior nuchal line - Landmark: ~1/3 of the distance from external occipital protuberance (inion) to the mastoid process - Lies MEDIAL to the occipital artery (palpate the artery to avoid intra-arterial injection) Lesser Occipita

nodes.title: Setup — Patient + Equipment
nodes.summary: Seated head-down or prone; 25-27 ga needle; bupivacaine 0.5% PLAIN 2-3 mL; steroid only for cervicogenic.
nodes.body: Patient position: - Seated with head flexed forward, forehead resting on a pillow (preferred), OR - Prone if cluster patient cannot tolerate sitting up Equipment: - 3 mL syringe - 25-27 gauge needle (1-1.5 inch / 25-38 mm) - Chlorhexidine or alcohol prep - Sterile gloves (clean technique acceptable; full sterile is overkill for a superficial peripheral block) - 2x2 gauze for hemostasis - Adhesive

nodes.title: Step 1 — Identify + Mark Landmarks
nodes.summary: 1/3 inion-mastoid for GON; medial to occipital artery pulse; 2/3 distance for LON.
nodes.body: 1. Palpate the external occipital protuberance (inion) — bony midline prominence at the back of the head. 2. Palpate the mastoid process — bony prominence behind the ear. 3. Draw an imaginary line between them along the superior nuchal line. 4. Mark a point ~1/3 of the distance from inion to mastoid — this is the GON target. 5. Palpate for the occipital artery pulse at this point. The GON lies MED

nodes.title: Step 2 — Inject
nodes.summary: Contact bone, withdraw 1-2 mm, ASPIRATE, inject 2-3 mL slowly.
nodes.body: 1. Hold the syringe perpendicular to the skull. 2. Advance the needle slowly until you contact bone (skull is the safety stop — prevents intracranial penetration). 3. Withdraw 1-2 mm off bone. 4. ASPIRATE before injecting. If blood returns → withdraw, redirect 1-2 mm medially, re-aspirate. Intra-arterial injection into the occipital artery (which feeds into the vertebral system via collaterals) ca

nodes.title: Aspirate Returned Blood — What Now?
nodes.body: You aspirated before injecting (good) and got blood return. The occipital artery runs near the GON target. Do NOT inject at this position.

nodes.title: Post-procedure Care
nodes.summary: Observe 15 min, document neuro exam, onset 5-15 min, LA 4-6h, return for fever/deficit/expanding hematoma.
nodes.body: Immediate: - Observe for 15 min for vasovagal syncope (1-3% incidence) - Document baseline + post-procedure neuro exam (especially the GON sensory distribution — occiput, vertex, posterior scalp) - Onset of relief: 5-15 minutes for cluster - LA-only duration: 4-6 hours (bupivacaine) or 1-2 hours (lidocaine) - LA + steroid duration: weeks to months (for cervicogenic / hemicrania continua) Discharge

nodes.title: Complications + Recognition
nodes.summary: Vasovagal 1-3%, intra-arterial → seizure/deficit, alopecia/Cushingoid with steroid.
nodes.body: Common (1-5%): - Vasovagal syncope — preventable with supine positioning post-procedure + 15 min observation - Local soreness 1-2 days - Transient occipital numbness extending beyond intended duration Uncommon but serious: - Intra-arterial injection (occipital artery → vertebral collateral) — can cause seizure, transient neurologic deficit, or stroke. PREVENT by aspirating before every injection.

nodes.title: Procedure Note Template
nodes.summary: Procedure note must capture: indication, consent, landmarks, agent, aspiration, response, observation, dispo.
nodes.body: Procedure: Greater occipital nerve block, [right/left/bilateral] Indication: [Cluster headache acute attack / Cluster bridge / Occipital neuralgia / Cervicogenic HA / Post-traumatic HA / Status migrainosus refractory] Consent: Verbal informed consent obtained; risks of vasovagal, transient numbness, intra-arterial injection, infection, alopecia (if steroid) discussed; patient agrees to proceed. nodes.title: Ocular POCUS: When and Why
nodes.summary: Indications: acute vision loss, trauma (exclude rupture first), elevated ICP, cannot visualize fundus; ABSOLUTE CI: suspected globe rupture
nodes.body: Ocular ultrasound is a rapid, bedside tool for diagnosing vision-threatening emergencies when direct visualization is limited. Indications: • Acute vision loss of unknown etiology • Eye trauma assessment (if globe rupture excluded) • Suspected elevated ICP • Cannot visualize fundus (hyphema, cataract, vitreous hemorrhage) • Suspected retinal detachment Absolute Contraindication: ⚠️ SUSPECTED GLOBE

nodes.title: Probe Selection & Technique
nodes.summary: High-frequency linear probe 7.5-15 MHz, copious gel standoff, MINIMAL pressure, transverse (marker temporal) and longitudinal planes, depth 4-5cm
nodes.body: Equipment: • High-frequency linear probe (7.5-15 MHz) • Higher frequency = better resolution for superficial structures • Acoustic standoff: thick layer of gel or Tegaderm over closed lid Patient Position: • Supine with eyes closed • Ask patient to look straight ahead (reduces movement artifact) • May ask to look in different directions to assess detachments Scanning Technique: | Plane | Orientati

nodes.summary: Scan 6 structures systematically: anterior chamber, iris/pupil, lens, vitreous, retina, optic nerve — dynamic assessment differentiates PVD from RD

Iris & Pupil | Shape, position | | 3. Lens | Position (dislocation?), clarity | | 4. Vitreous | Echogenicity (normally anechoic) | | 5. Retina | Attachment, detachment | | 6. Optic Nerve | ONSD measurement | Dynamic Assessment: • Have pati

nodes.title: Normal Ocular Anatomy
nodes.summary: Normal: anechoic vitreous, biconvex lens, retina adherent to wall — any echogenicity in vitreous is abnormal

nodes.title: What Are You Evaluating For?
nodes.summary: Select primary indication: vision loss/floaters (RD vs PVD), elevated ICP (ONSD), eye trauma, or CRAO
