nodes.title: Cervical spine evaluation
nodes.body: Use NEXUS or Canadian C-Spine Rule to determine need for imaging: - NEXUS: no midline tenderness, no focal neuro deficit, normal alertness, no intoxication, no distracting injury → no imaging. - Canadian C-Spine: age >65, dangerous mechanism, paresthesias → image. Otherwise low-risk factors permit clinical clearance. If any criterion fails → maintain immobilization, CT cervical spine. MRI if persi

nodes.title: Shoulder injury — pattern
nodes.body: Identify the dominant pattern.

nodes.title: Focused shoulder exam
nodes.body: Inspection: asymmetry, deformity, swelling. Palpation: AC joint, sternoclavicular joint, biceps groove, greater tuberosity. ROM: active forward flexion, abduction, internal/external rotation. Pain arc 60–120° → impingement; pain at end-range → AC joint. Provocative tests: Neer, Hawkins-Kennedy (impingement); empty can (supraspinatus); apprehension/relocation (anterior instability); cross-body addu

nodes.title: AC joint sprain (Rockwood I–VI)
nodes.body: Direct blow or fall on adducted shoulder → AC joint injury graded I–VI by Rockwood: - I: sprain, no deformity → sling 1–2 wk, NSAIDs, early ROM - II: AC ligament torn, coracoclavicular intact, mild step-off → sling 2–3 wk - III: both ligaments torn, prominent distal clavicle → sling, conservative trial; surgery if persistent symptoms or laborer/athlete - IV–VI: posterior, severe inferior, or pancl

nodes.title: Rotator cuff tendinopathy / tear
nodes.body: Tendinopathy (overuse): pain with overhead activity, painful arc, positive Neer/Hawkins. Treatment: relative rest, NSAIDs, structured PT (4–6 wk). Acute tear (often after fall or sudden lift): weakness with empty can / external rotation, drop arm sign. MRI for diagnosis if conservative trial fails or weakness severe. Disposition: sling for comfort, NSAIDs, sports medicine or orthopedics follow-up

nodes.title: Clavicle fracture
nodes.body: Most fractures (middle third, <100% displaced, <2 cm shortening): sling, ice, NSAIDs, early ROM at 2 wk, ortho follow-up. Surgical indications: - Open fracture - Skin tenting / threat - Neurovascular compromise - Distal third with coracoclavicular ligament disruption - Significant displacement (>2 cm shortening) in athlete or laborer Obtain AP and 30° cephalad films. Examine for pneumothorax (rib/

nodes.title: When to image the shoulder
nodes.body: Plain films (AP + axillary or scapular Y): - Trauma with deformity, suspected fracture, suspected dislocation - Persistent symptoms after 2–3 weeks of conservative care MRI: - Suspected rotator cuff tear with weakness - Suspected labral injury (recurrent dislocations, mechanical symptoms) - Persistent pain after normal X-ray and conservative trial ED MRI rarely indicated for sports shoulder injuri

nodes.title: Knee injury — Ottawa Knee Rule first
nodes.body: Ottawa Knee Rule — image the knee if any of: - Age ≥55 - Isolated patellar tenderness - Tenderness at fibular head - Inability to flex to 90° - Inability to bear weight (4 steps) immediately AND in ED Use the calculator to score this patient.

nodes.title: Knee plain films + targeted exam
nodes.body: AP, lateral, and skyline patellar views. Add tibial plateau views if posterolateral pain or high-energy mechanism (Lipscomb sign). If fracture present: - Tibial plateau / patella displaced → orthopedics - Avulsion fragment with knee instability → consider Segond fracture (pathognomonic for ACL tear) - Open fracture → see vascular pathway If no fracture but clinically unstable (positive Lachman or

nodes.title: Knee exam — special tests
nodes.body: Mechanism + tests narrow the differential: - Pop + immediate effusion + giving way → ACL - Twisting + locking + joint-line tenderness → meniscus - Direct lateral blow + medial pain → MCL - Hyperextension + posterior pain → PCL - Patellar dislocation history → patellofemoral instability Key tests: Lachman (most sensitive for ACL), McMurray (meniscus), valgus/varus stress, posterior drawer, patellar

nodes.title: ACL tear — ED management
nodes.body: Ottawa rules positive or normal X-ray: rest, ice, NSAIDs, knee immobilizer, crutches, weight-bear as tolerated. Outpatient MRI within 1 week and orthopedics referral. Do not promise return-to-play timeline in the ED — surgical management (BTB or hamstring graft) typically requires 6–9 months of rehab. Some non-pivoting athletes manage non-operatively. Pearl: Segond fracture on plain film = ACL tea

nodes.title: Meniscus injury
nodes.body: Findings: joint-line tenderness, positive McMurray, locked knee (mechanical block to extension). ED workup: plain films to rule out fracture; if locked, prompt orthopedic consult — may need urgent surgical reduction. Disposition (non-locked): rest, ice, NSAIDs, range-of-motion exercises, outpatient MRI and ortho referral within 1–2 weeks.[10]

nodes.title: Collateral ligament sprain (MCL/LCL)
nodes.body: Graded I (sprain) → III (complete tear). Treatment: - Grade I/II: hinged knee brace, weight-bear as tolerated, NSAIDs, PT, return to sport in 2–6 weeks. - Grade III: brace at 30° flexion, ortho referral; surgical repair occasionally needed (especially LCL with posterolateral corner injury). Pearl: isolated LCL injuries are rare — always evaluate posterolateral corner with PCL when LCL torn.[10]

nodes.title: Patellar dislocation
nodes.body: Reduction: extend knee + medial pressure on patella. Procedural sedation rarely needed. Post-reduction films (AP, lateral, skyline) to evaluate for osteochondral fracture. MRI if locked, hemarthrosis, or recurrent. Disposition: knee immobilizer in extension, weight-bear as tolerated, outpatient orthopedics within 1 week, PT for VMO strengthening.[10]

nodes.title: Ankle injury — Ottawa Ankle Rule
nodes.body: Ottawa Ankle Rule — image if any of: - Bone tenderness at posterior edge or tip of either malleolus - Bone tenderness at base of 5th metatarsal or navicular (foot rule) - Inability to bear weight 4 steps immediately AND in ED Sensitivity ~98% for clinically significant fractures.

nodes.title: Ankle / foot imaging interpretation
nodes.body: Ankle: AP, lateral, mortise. Foot: AP, lateral, oblique. Critical fractures to recognize: - Maisonneuve fracture (proximal fibula + medial malleolus / deltoid disruption) — palpate proximal fibula on every ankle injury - Lisfranc injury (tarsometatarsal disruption) — tenderness at base of 1st/2nd MT, weight-bearing films, MRI/CT if subtle - Jones fracture (5th MT base, proximal diaphysis) — high n

nodes.title: Ankle sprain
nodes.body: Most are lateral ankle sprains (ATFL > CFL > PTFL). Treatment: - PRICE: protection, relative rest, ice, compression, elevation - Functional bracing or lace-up brace (better than rigid immobilization for return-to-sport) - Weight-bear as tolerated - Early ROM + proprioception PT - NSAIDs short course High ankle sprain (syndesmosis): squeeze test positive, external rotation pain — longer recovery, m

nodes.title: Pediatric athlete — physeal considerations
nodes.body: Open growth plates change everything: - Ligaments are stronger than physes — what looks like a "sprain" in an adult may be a Salter-Harris fracture in a child. - Tenderness at the physis on plain film (or even with negative X-ray) → treat as Salter-Harris I and immobilize. - Apophyseal injuries (Osgood-Schlatter, Sever, Little League shoulder/elbow) are overuse — relative rest, gradual return.[13]

nodes.title: Salter-Harris classification
nodes.body: Mnemonic SALTR: - S — Slipped (I): through physis only — often radiographically occult - A — Above (II): through physis + metaphysis (most common) - L — Lower (III): through physis + epiphysis (intra-articular) - T — Through (IV): through physis, metaphysis, epiphysis (intra-articular) - R — Ruined (V): crush injury — worst prognosis for growth Disposition: - I & II: closed reduction + immobilizat

nodes.title: Apophysitis / overuse syndromes
nodes.body: - Osgood-Schlatter (tibial tubercle apophysitis): pain at tibial tubercle in adolescent. Treatment: relative rest, ice, NSAIDs, quad/hamstring stretching. Resolves with skeletal maturity. - Sever disease (calcaneal apophysitis): heel pain in active 8–14 year-old. Treatment: relative rest, heel cup, calf stretching. - Little League elbow (medial epicondyle apophysitis): pain in pitching arm. STOP T

nodes.title: Stress fracture — adolescent athlete
nodes.body: Sports-driven stress fractures (tibia, metatarsals, navicular, femoral neck, pars interarticularis) appear in adolescent runners and gymnasts. Workup: plain films often negative for 2–4 weeks; MRI is gold standard for early diagnosis. High-risk locations (need urgent ortho): - Femoral neck (tension side, superior cortex) - Anterior tibial cortex ("dreaded black line") - Navicular - Talus, 5th MT b

nodes.title: Disposition and follow-up
nodes.body: ED pearls: - Splint or sling for comfort, NSAIDs, ice, elevation - Crutches if NWB - Ortho or sports medicine follow-up — concussions ideally to a concussion clinic - Strict return precautions (worsening pain, neurovascular changes, fever, increased swelling) - Discuss timeline expectations — sports injuries rarely resolve in days For concussion specifically, discharge instructions should include

nodes.title: Return-to-play general checklist
nodes.body: A patient is ready to return to play when: - Full pain-free ROM - Strength symmetric to uninjured side (≥90%) - No swelling at rest or after activity - Sport-specific functional testing (cutting, jumping) without symptoms - Cleared by treating clinician (concussion: cleared by physician familiar with concussion management) Criteria are joint- and sport-specific — refer to sports medicine for defin

nodes.title: Pitfalls in sports injury workup
nodes.body: 1. Missing the proximal fibula in ankle injuries — Maisonneuve fracture goes home as "ankle sprain" 2. Calling pediatric extremity tenderness "sprain" — physes fail before ligaments 3. Discharging concussion without explicit RTP plan — second-impact syndrome can be fatal 4. Returning ACL-injured athlete to play same day — knee instability + cutting = catastrophic re-injury 5. Ignoring posterolater

nodes.title: Summary card
nodes.body: Sports injury workup at a glance: - Triage red flags first: head, c-spine, vascular, dislocation - Decision rules save imaging: Ottawa Knee, Ottawa Ankle, NEXUS, Canadian C-Spine - Concussion → relative rest 24-48h, early symptom-limited activity, then six-step RTP with no same-day return - Knee + ACL → Lachman is most sensitive; Segond = ACL - Maisonneuve → palpate proximal fibula on every ankle

nodes.title: Status Epilepticus
nodes.summary: SE defined as seizure >5 min or recurrent without recovery — check eyes for BAO mimic BEFORE BZD algorithm
nodes.body: > 🚨 BEFORE YOU START THE BZD ALGORITHM: LOOK AT THE EYES. > Basilar artery occlusion (BAO) can mimic refractory SE — convulsive movements, posturing, hyperekplexia, and coma with no cortical EEG correlate. Median time from ED arrival to BAO diagnosis when it presents this way is 8h 24min, and only 19% are caught inside the tPA window. BAO mortality without recanalization is ~75%. > 👉 Quick BAO m

nodes.title: 60-Second BAO Mimicker Check — Look at the Eyes
nodes.summary: Eyes are the brainstem window — dysconjugate, skew, vertical palsy, bobbing, fixed pupils, absent doll's eyes = BAO
nodes.body: Dell Med pearl: A "seizure" that won't respond to Ativan until you chemically coma them is BASILAR until proven otherwise. The brainstem is the eyes' window. In SE the brainstem is intact, so eyes still move conjugately, doll's eyes work, pupils are reactive. In BAO the brainstem is structurally wrecked — eyes give it away in 60 seconds. Quick exam — answer YES if ANY of these are present: • Dysco

nodes.title: Pivot: Basilar Artery Occlusion Suspected
nodes.summary: Stop SE workup, CTA STAT, activate neuro-IR, thrombectomy up to 24h (BAOCHE/ATTENTION), permissive HTN
nodes.body: Stop chasing SE. Get the CTA. Call neuro-IR. BAO presenting as convulsive movements / refractory "SE" is a known and lethal trap. Median time to diagnosis when it presents this way is 8h 24min — only 19% caught inside the tPA window (Liu 2022 systematic review). Mortality without recanalization ~75% (StatPearls; ATTENTION/BAOCHE control arms). --- 📋 Immediate actions: 1. CTA head and neck STAT —
nodes.recommendation: Stop SE escalation. CTA head/neck STAT, activate neuro-IR, permissive HTN, test for locked-in with vertical gaze. Thrombectomy window up to 24h from LKW (BAOCHE/ATTENTION).

nodes.title: Is This Status Epilepticus?
nodes.summary: Differentiate convulsive SE, subtle SE, NCSE, and mimics — duration, motor features, and consciousness guide triage
nodes.body: Convulsive SE: Generalized tonic-clonic activity >5 min, or recurrent seizures without recovery of consciousness between episodes. Subtle / late SE: After prolonged generalized seizure, motor activity may diminish — look for subtle signs: facial twitching, nystagmus, eye deviation. Key history: Duration of seizure activity, witnessed motor features, prior seizure history, current medications, rece

nodes.title: ABCs & Initial Stabilization
nodes.summary: Left lateral position, high-flow O2, dual IV access, start the clock — no bite block, no restraints
nodes.body: Airway: Position in left lateral decubitus if actively seizing. Suction available. Nasopharyngeal airway if needed — do NOT use bite block or oral airway (risk of obstruction and provider injury). Do NOT attempt intubation during active tonic-clonic seizure unless airway compromise. Breathing: High-flow O2 via non-rebreather. Monitor SpO2 continuously. Respiratory failure can occur from seizure it

nodes.title: Glucose & Diagnostic Workup
nodes.summary: Fingerstick glucose STAT — D50W if <60; labs, CT, EEG; 48% of altered post-SE have ongoing NCSE
nodes.body: Fingerstick glucose STAT — hypoglycemia is a common, easily reversible seizure trigger. • If glucose <60 mg/dL: D50W 25 g IV (adults) or D10W 2-5 mL/kg (peds) SE Diagnostic Workup — complete lab panel and imaging guide. Priority labs: BMP (Na, Ca, Mg, Phos), CBC, lactate, VBG, urine drug screen, serum tox, ASM levels (if on therapy), troponin, CK, pregnancy test. Imaging: CT head non-contrast afte

nodes.title: IV Access Available?
nodes.summary: Route determines BZD choice — IV lorazepam preferred, IM midazolam if no IV (RAMPART: non-inferior)
nodes.body: Route of administration determines first-line benzodiazepine choice. IV access preferred but should NOT delay treatment. If IV is not immediately available, give IM midazolam — the RAMPART trial showed IM midazolam is non-inferior to IV lorazepam and faster to administer. Underdosing of benzodiazepines leads to poor response and increased likelihood of refractory SE.

nodes.title: IV Lorazepam (First-Line)
nodes.summary: Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV max 4 mg, repeat once in 5-10 min — monitor respiratory depression
nodes.body: Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg/dose), push over 2 min. May repeat once in 5-10 minutes if seizure persists. Total max: 8 mg. Alternative if lorazepam unavailable: • Diazepam 0.15-0.2 mg/kg IV (max 10 mg), repeat once Lorazepam is preferred over diazepam — higher seizure termination rate (65% vs 56%) and longer duration of action. Monitor for respiratory depression — have bag-valve mask and sucti

nodes.title: IM Midazolam (No IV Access)
nodes.summary: Midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IM max 10 mg — RAMPART showed 73% termination; continue seeking IV access
nodes.body: Midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IM (max 10 mg) into deltoid or vastus lateralis. RAMPART trial: IM midazolam terminated seizures in 73% vs 63% for IV lorazepam (p<.001). Faster time to treatment offset the slightly slower IM onset. Weight-based dosing: • ≥40 kg: 10 mg IM • 13-40 kg: 5 mg IM Alternative routes: • Intranasal midazolam: 0.2 mg/kg via mucosal atomizer (less effective than IM per Guterman et al) •

nodes.title: Seizure Response to Benzodiazepine?
nodes.summary: Assess 5 min after BZD — cessation of motor activity AND improving consciousness means success
nodes.body: Assess 5 minutes after BZD administration. Up to 2 doses of first-line BZD may be given. If second dose given, reassess after 5 additional minutes. Seizure terminated = cessation of all motor activity AND progressive improvement in consciousness. Subtle motor signs (facial twitching, nystagmus) may indicate ongoing SE.

nodes.title: Seizure Terminated After Benzodiazepine
nodes.body: Seizure terminated with first-line benzodiazepine therapy. Post-seizure management: • Monitor for recurrence — recurrence risk is significant • Complete diagnostic workup (labs, imaging, EEG if available) • Determine etiology — drives 80% of outcome • Consider ASM loading for seizure prophylaxis if first unprovoked seizure with high recurrence risk, known epilepsy with subtherapeutic levels, or st
nodes.recommendation: Seizure terminated with BZD. Monitor for recurrence, complete etiology workup. Load maintenance ASM if indicated. If no return to baseline within 30-60 min, obtain EEG to rule out NCSE.

nodes.title: Special Population?
nodes.summary: Screen for pregnancy, toxic ingestion, or pediatric age before selecting 2nd-line ASM
nodes.body: Before selecting 2nd-line antiseizure medication, identify if the patient belongs to a special population that changes management. If none apply, proceed directly to standard 2nd-line ASM selection.

nodes.title: Second-Line ASM Selection
nodes.summary: ESETT: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, valproate equally effective (~47%) — choose by comorbidities
nodes.body: BZD-refractory convulsive SE. Administer within 5-10 minutes of BZD failure. ESETT trial (2019): Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, and valproate had equivalent efficacy (~47% seizure cessation at 60 min). No significant difference in adverse events between the three agents. Choice should be tailored to patient's comorbidities and contraindications. 2nd-Line ASM Comparison — side-by-side efficacy, contr

nodes.title: Levetiracetam (Keppra)
nodes.summary: Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV max 4500 mg — no cardiac effects, no drug interactions, safe in pregnancy
nodes.body: Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (max 4500 mg) over 10-15 min. ESETT: 47% seizure termination at 60 min (equivalent to fosphenytoin and valproate). Advantages: • No cardiac effects — no telemetry requirement during infusion • No hepatic metabolism — no drug interactions • Safe in renal impairment (dose adjust if CrCl <50) • Safe in pregnancy (Category C, low teratogenicity — preferred 2nd line in pregnan

nodes.title: Valproate Sodium (Depacon)
nodes.summary: Valproate 40 mg/kg IV max 3000 mg — contraindicated in pregnancy, liver disease, mitochondrial disorders
nodes.body: Valproate 40 mg/kg IV (max 3000 mg) over 10 min. ESETT: 46% seizure termination at 60 min. Contraindicated in: • Pregnancy (teratogenic — neural tube defects, Category X) • Hepatic disease / liver failure • Mitochondrial disorders (Alpers syndrome — fatal hepatotoxicity) • Known or suspected urea cycle disorders • Pancreatitis Cautions: • Thrombocytopenia / coagulopathy — check platelets • May cau

nodes.title: Fosphenytoin (Cerebyx)
nodes.summary: Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV — requires cardiac monitoring, INEFFECTIVE for drug/alcohol-induced seizures
nodes.body: Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV (max 1500 mg PE) at max rate 150 mg PE/min. ESETT: 45% seizure termination at 60 min. Requires cardiac monitoring during and for 20 min after infusion — risk of: • Hypotension • Cardiac arrhythmia (bradycardia, QT prolongation) • AV block INEFFECTIVE for drug/alcohol-induced seizures — phenytoin's selective action on voltage-gated sodium channels is insufficient for dif

nodes.title: 2nd-Line ASM Response?
nodes.summary: Assess 20 min after infusion — persistent seizure = refractory SE, 30-40% fail 2nd-line therapy
nodes.body: Assess 20 minutes after start of infusion. If seizure persists or recurs, this is now refractory status epilepticus (RSE). ~30-40% of patients fail 2nd-line therapy. As SE duration increases, GABAA receptor internalization progresses and benzodiazepine/ASM resistance increases. If the first 2nd-line agent fails, guidelines recommend either: • Adding another 2nd-line ASM, OR • Proceeding directly t

nodes.title: Phenobarbital
nodes.summary: Phenobarbital 15-20 mg/kg IV — high respiratory depression risk, have intubation ready
nodes.body: Phenobarbital 15-20 mg/kg IV at max rate 50-100 mg/min. Max single dose: 2000 mg. Use when ESETT agents (levetiracetam, valproate, fosphenytoin) are unavailable or contraindicated. Significant risks: • Respiratory depression — may precipitate need for intubation • Hypotension • Excessive sedation Have intubation supplies ready before administration. Also first-line for: • Neonatal seizures • Benzo

nodes.title: Seizure Terminated After 2nd-Line ASM
nodes.body: Seizure terminated with 2nd-line antiseizure medication. Critical: Monitor for NCSE — ESETT data showed 48% of patients with altered consciousness post-SE had ongoing nonconvulsive seizures on EEG. Post-seizure management: • Continuous EEG monitoring recommended — minimum 24h • Continue maintenance dosing of the ASM that terminated seizure • Complete etiology workup (labs, imaging, LP if indicated
nodes.recommendation: Seizure terminated with 2nd-line ASM. Admit to ICU. Continuous EEG monitoring × 24-48h recommended. Continue maintenance ASM. Complete etiology workup.

nodes.title: Refractory SE — Intubation & Preparation
nodes.summary: RSE requires intubation, arterial line, continuous EEG — short-acting paralytic for seizure assessment
nodes.body: Refractory SE (RSE) = failure of first-line BZD AND adequate second-line ASM. Occurs in ~30-40% of SE presentations. Immediate actions: • Secure airway with rapid sequence intubation • Avoid prolonged paralysis — use short-acting agent (succinylcholine preferred over rocuronium) to allow clinical seizure assessment • Arterial line for continuous BP monitoring • Central venous access for vasopresso

nodes.title: RSE — Continuous Infusion Selection
nodes.summary: Select continuous infusion for EEG burst suppression — midazolam, propofol, pentobarbital, or ketamine
nodes.body: Goal: EEG seizure suppression or burst suppression for 24-48 hours before weaning attempt. No large RCTs demonstrate clear superiority between agents. Choice based on clinical factors. All agents require mechanical ventilation and ICU-level care. Continuous Infusion Comparison — dosing, hemodynamic effects, and unique risks for each agent.

nodes.title: RSE/SRSE Monitoring & Weaning
nodes.summary: Maintain burst suppression 24-48h, wean 25% q4-6h — SRSE if seizures persist despite 24h anesthesia
nodes.body: Continuous EEG targets: • Burst suppression (3-10 sec bursts, <50% suppression ratio) • OR complete seizure suppression (depending on clinical scenario) Maintenance: 24-48 hours of seizure suppression before first wean attempt. Weaning protocol: • Reduce infusion by 25% every 4-6 hours with continuous EEG • If seizures recur on wean → restart at effective dose, extend 24h, retry Super-refractory S

nodes.title: Disposition & Ongoing Management
nodes.body: All SE patients require ICU admission. Monitoring: • Continuous EEG monitoring × minimum 24-48h • Detect NCSE, guide treatment, monitor for recurrence Workup to complete: • MRI brain (when stable) — superior to CT for structural causes • LP if infectious or autoimmune etiology suspected • Autoimmune encephalitis panel if no clear etiology (NMDA-receptor Ab, LGI1, CASPR2) • ASM levels (therapeutic
nodes.recommendation: Admit to ICU. Continuous EEG × 24-48h. Complete etiology workup (MRI, LP if indicated, autoimmune panel if cryptogenic). Continue maintenance ASM. Neurology consultation.

nodes.title: Pregnancy / Eclampsia
nodes.summary: Eclampsia: MgSO4 first; epilepsy in pregnancy: prefer levetiracetam, AVOID valproate (Category X)
nodes.body: First question: Is this eclampsia or epilepsy? Eclampsia if: hypertension, proteinuria, edema, >20 weeks gestation, or new-onset seizure in pregnancy without prior seizure history. Eclampsia treatment: • Magnesium Sulfate 4-6 g IV over 15-20 min, then 1-2 g/hr infusion • If seizures persist despite magnesium → benzodiazepines (lorazepam) • OB consultation STAT — consider emergent delivery • Fetal

nodes.title: Substance-Induced SE
nodes.summary: INH toxicity: pyridoxine 5g IV empiric; alcohol withdrawal: BZDs + phenobarbital; phenytoin INEFFECTIVE for drug-induced SE
nodes.body: 9% of SE cases are substance-induced. Isoniazid (INH) toxicity: • Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is the specific antidote • Dose: gram-for-gram to amount ingested, OR 5 g IV empiric if amount unknown • INH depletes pyridoxine → GABA synthesis fails → refractory seizures • Standard ASMs are ineffective without pyridoxine Alcohol withdrawal: • Benzodiazepines are first-line (high-dose may be needed) • Phen

nodes.title: Pediatric Considerations
nodes.summary: Same algorithm as adults with weight-based dosing — consider pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy in neonates/infants
nodes.body: Same treatment algorithm as adults — BZD first-line, then 2nd-line ASM, then anesthetic infusions. BZD dosing (weight-based): • IV Lorazepam: 0.1 mg/kg (max 4 mg), repeat × 1 • IM Midazolam: 13-40 kg → 5 mg; ≥40 kg → 10 mg (0.2 mg/kg, max 10 mg) • Rectal Diazepam: 0.2-0.5 mg/kg (max 20 mg) 2nd-line ASM: Same agents and weight-based dosing as adults (per ESETT, which included pediatric patients). •

nodes.title: Nonconvulsive Status Epilepticus (NCSE)
nodes.summary: NCSE in 48% of altered post-SE patients — requires EEG for diagnosis, BZD trial is diagnostic + therapeutic
nodes.body: NCSE accounts for up to 48% of patients with altered consciousness post-SE (ESETT data). Suspect NCSE if: • Unexplained altered mental status after convulsive SE • Subtle motor signs: eye deviation, nystagmus, lip smacking, eyelid fluttering, myoclonus • Failure to return to baseline after initial seizure treatment • Acutely ill ICU patients (especially on neurotoxic medications: cephalosporins, m

nodes.title: Not SE — Differential Diagnosis
nodes.body: Common SE mimics: • Psychogenic nonepileptic seizures (PNES): Most common mimic. Features suggesting PNES: side-to-side head movements, pelvic thrusting, forced eye closure (seizures: eyes open), emotional outbursts, asynchronous limb movements, waxing/waning pattern, absence of postictal confusion. Video EEG is definitive. • Syncope with myoclonus: Brief jerking movements after loss of consciousn
nodes.recommendation: Consider alternative diagnosis. If uncertain, treat as SE until proven otherwise. PNES is the most common mimic — video EEG is definitive. Do not administer antiseizure medications for confirmed PNES.

nodes.title: Suspect STEMI
nodes.summary: 12-lead ECG within 10 min — STEMI is an ECG diagnosis, do NOT wait for troponin; 8.4% ACS without chest pain
nodes.body: STEMI Steps Summary Obtain 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact. Classic presentation: chest pain/pressure \u00B1 radiation to arms, jaw, or back, with diaphoresis, nausea/vomiting, or dyspnea. High-risk features: \u2022 Chest pain + diaphoresis = highest likelihood ratio for STEMI [1] \u2022 Radiation to both arms \u2014 96% specific (but only 11% sensitive) [2] \u2022 8.4% of A

nodes.title: ECG Pattern Assessment
nodes.summary: Apply STEMI criteria to 12-lead — STE in ≥2 contiguous leads, check V2-V3 sex/age thresholds, look for reciprocal changes
nodes.body: STEMI criteria: New J-point elevation in \u22652 contiguous leads: \u2022 \u22651 mm in all leads EXCEPT V2-V3 \u2022 V2-V3: \u22652 mm in men \u226540y, \u22652.5 mm in men <40y, \u22651.5 mm in women Also look for reciprocal changes \u2014 PAILS Mnemonic What does the 12-lead ECG show?

nodes.title: STEMI Confirmed \u2014 Activate Cath Lab
nodes.summary: Activate cath lab immediately — identify territory by STE distribution; inferior STEMI needs right-sided leads
nodes.body: Immediately activate cardiac catheterization laboratory. Identify territory by STE distribution: \u2022 Anterior: V1-V4 \u2014 LAD occlusion \u2022 Inferior: II, III, aVF \u2014 RCA (85%) or LCx (15%) \u2022 Lateral: I, aVL, V5, V6 \u2014 LCx occlusion \u2022 Posterior: V7-V9 STE (\u00B1 V1-V3 ST depression) \u2014 LCx If inferior STEMI: Get right-sided leads to assess for RV involvement (\u2192 a

nodes.title: Evaluate for Posterior STEMI
nodes.summary: V1-V3 depression with upright T waves — obtain posterior leads V7-V9, STE ≥0.5 mm confirms posterior STEMI
nodes.body: ST depression in V1-V3 with upright T waves and prominent R wave suggests posterior (inferobasal) STEMI. Obtain posterior leads V7, V8, V9: \u2022 V7 \u2014 posterior axillary line at level of V6 \u2022 V8 \u2014 tip of scapula \u2022 V9 \u2014 halfway between V8 and left paraspinal muscles Diagnostic criteria: STE \u22650.5 mm in any posterior lead (\u22651 mm in men <40y has higher specificity)

nodes.title: LBBB / Paced Rhythm \u2014 Sgarbossa Criteria
nodes.summary: Apply Sgarbossa/modified Smith criteria in LBBB — score ≥3 = 98% specific; LBBB + ischemic symptoms = manage as STEMI
nodes.body: In LBBB or ventricular pacing, standard STEMI criteria cannot be applied. Use Sgarbossa Criteria to evaluate. Sgarbossa Criteria (any ONE positive = STEMI): \u2022 Concordant STE \u22651 mm in leads with positive QRS (5 pts) \u2022 Concordant ST depression \u22651 mm in V1-V3 (3 pts) \u2022 Discordant STE \u22655 mm in leads with negative QRS (2 pts) Modified Sgarbossa (Smith criteria): \u2022 Rep

nodes.title: aVR Elevation \u2014 Left Main Concern
nodes.summary: aVR STE + diffuse depression — only 10% are acute thrombotic occlusion; hemodynamic instability favors emergent cath
nodes.body: STE in aVR with \u22651 mm ST depression in multiple leads may suggest: \u2022 Left main coronary artery stenosis or occlusion \u2022 Triple vessel disease \u2022 Diffuse subendocardial ischemia Important: Only 10% of patients with this pattern have acute thrombotic coronary occlusion. [11] Clinical context is critical. Assess hemodynamic status \u2014 instability strongly favors emergent catheter

nodes.title: Serial ECGs & Continued Monitoring
nodes.summary: Serial ECGs q15-30 min — 8% of STEMIs identified only on repeat; bedside echo 93% sensitive for RWMA
nodes.body: Obtain serial ECGs at 15- to 30-minute intervals for the first 1\u20132 hours. \u2022 8% of all STEMIs are identified only on repeat ECG [12] \u2022 Dynamic ST changes are expected in evolving AMI \u2022 Use fixed electrode positions for comparison Consider bedside echo: RWMA present in 93% of AMI patients (but also in 43% without AMI \u2014 sensitive but not specific) [13] STEMI is an ECG diagnos

nodes.title: NSTEMI / ACS Workup
nodes.body: STEMI criteria not met but ACS remains on differential. \u2022 Serial troponins q3\u20136h \u2022 Continuous cardiac monitoring \u2022 Aspirin 162\u2013325 mg if not already given \u2022 Consider anticoagulation per NSTEMI protocol \u2022 Consult cardiology for risk stratification See NSTEMI Management for full NSTEMI decision pathway.
nodes.recommendation: Manage as NSTEMI/ACS. Serial troponins, cardiology consult, risk stratification. See NSTEMI consult for detailed management.

nodes.title: Alternative Diagnosis
nodes.body: ST elevation identified as non-ACS etiology. Common STEMI mimics: \u2022 Pericarditis \u2014 diffuse concave STE, PR depression, no reciprocal changes \u2022 Hyperkalemia \u2014 peaked T waves, wide QRS, pseudo-STEMI pattern \u2022 Left ventricular hypertrophy \u2014 strain pattern \u2022 Benign early repolarization \u2022 Takotsubo cardiomyopathy \u2014 apical ballooning \u2022 Brugada syndrome S
nodes.recommendation: Treat underlying condition. Maintain index of suspicion for ACS if clinical picture evolves.

nodes.title: Initial Medical Therapy
nodes.summary: ASA 162-325 mg chewed, NTG SL (avoid if SBP<90/RV infarct/PDE5i), O2 only if SpO2<90, avoid morphine
nodes.body: Start simultaneously with cath lab activation: Antiplatelet: \u2022 Aspirin 162\u2013325 mg chewed (if not given prehospital) \u2022 P2Y12 inhibitor loading \u2014 select agent next Pain / Symptom management: \u2022 Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL q5min \u00D7 3 (avoid if SBP <90, suspected RV infarct, or PDE-5 inhibitor use within 24\u201348h) \u2022 O\u2082 only if SpO\u2082 <90% \u2014 routine O\u2082

nodes.title: P2Y12 Inhibitor Selection
nodes.summary: Prasugrel and ticagrelor Class I equivalent for PCI (2025 ACC/AHA); clopidogrel for fibrinolysis or if others CI
nodes.body: Load with ONE P2Y12 inhibitor before or at time of PCI. Discuss with interventional cardiologist. Prasugrel 60 mg loading \u2192 10 mg daily \u2022 More potent platelet inhibition, lower ischemic events vs clopidogrel; ticagrelor and prasugrel are Class I equivalents (no preference) in 2025 ACC/AHA [18][23] \u2022 CONTRAINDICATED: prior stroke/TIA \u2014 basis: TRITON-TIMI 38 (n=13,608), where pat

nodes.title: Anticoagulation
nodes.summary: UFH 70-100 units/kg for PCI; bivalirudin if high bleeding risk; enoxaparin for fibrinolysis
nodes.body: For primary PCI: \u2022 UFH 70\u2013100 units/kg IV bolus (without GP IIb/IIIa) OR 50\u201370 units/kg (with GP IIb/IIIa) \u2022 Bivalirudin 0.75 mg/kg IV bolus then 1.75 mg/kg/hr \u2014 preferred if high bleeding risk For fibrinolytic therapy (minimum 48 hours): \u2022 UFH weight-based bolus + infusion \u2022 Enoxaparin \u2014 alternative (age-adjusted dosing) \u2022 Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC daily

nodes.title: Reperfusion Strategy
nodes.summary: PCI preferred — FMC-to-device ≤90 min local, ≤120 min transfer; fibrinolytics if PCI not available within 120 min
nodes.body: Primary PCI is preferred over fibrinolysis. See Reperfusion Decision Pathway Time targets: \u2022 FMC-to-device \u226490 min at PCI-capable facility \u2022 FMC-to-device \u2264120 min for transfer patients \u2022 DIDO (door-in\u2013door-out) \u226430 min at referring hospital \u2022 Door-to-needle \u226430 min for fibrinolytics Is PCI available within target timeframes?

nodes.title: Primary PCI
nodes.summary: Primary PCI for onset <12h; 12-24h if ongoing ischemia; >24h stable = PCI NOT recommended
nodes.body: Goal: First medical contact-to-device \u226490 minutes. \u2022 Indicated for symptom onset <12 hours [5][23] \u2022 Between 12\u201324 hours: reasonable if clinical or ECG evidence of ongoing ischemia [5][23] \u2022 >24 hours, asymptomatic, stable: PCI NOT recommended (no benefit) \u2014 basis is the OAT trial, which found no reduction in death, reinfarction, or class IV heart failure with late PC

nodes.title: Transfer for PCI
nodes.summary: DIDO ≤30 min; consider helicopter; switch to fibrinolysis if transfer cannot achieve 120 min
nodes.body: Goal: Total FMC-to-device \u2264120 minutes. DIDO \u226430 minutes. \u2022 Consider helicopter EMS to reduce transport time \u2022 Continue anticoagulation during transport \u2022 Prehospital cath lab activation reduces FMC-to-balloon time \u2022 Bypass non-PCI facilities if transport time <30 min to PCI center [5] If transfer cannot achieve 120 min: Switch to fibrinolytic strategy. Cardiogenic sh

nodes.title: Fibrinolytic Therapy
nodes.summary: Door-to-needle ≤30 min — tenecteplase preferred; half-dose if >75y; check contraindications first
nodes.body: Door-to-needle \u226430 minutes. Fibrin-specific agents preferred. Check Fibrinolytic Contraindications Agents (see Fibrinolytic Dosing): \u2022 Tenecteplase \u2014 single weight-based IV bolus (preferred) \u2022 Alteplase \u2014 accelerated 90-min regimen \u2022 Reteplase \u2014 10 + 10 unit double bolus Age >75 years: Consider half-dose tenecteplase (reduced ICH risk) \u2014 basis: STREAM-1 halv

nodes.title: Post-Fibrinolysis Management
nodes.summary: Anticoag ≥48h post-lytics; transfer for PCI in 3-24h (NOT within first 2-3h); AIVR is benign — do NOT treat
nodes.body: After administering fibrinolytic: 1. Anticoagulation (minimum 48 hours): [5][8][23] \u2022 UFH weight-based bolus + infusion, OR \u2022 Enoxaparin (age-adjusted) \u2014 age-adjusted regimen and superiority over 48h UFH established in ExTRACT-TIMI 25 (n=20,506; death or nonfatal reinfarction 9.9% vs 12.0%, at the cost of more major bleeding) [34] \u2022 Fondaparinux 2.5 mg SC daily [5][8] 2. Transf

nodes.title: Complications Assessment
nodes.summary: Screen for cardiogenic shock, RV involvement, reperfusion arrhythmias, AV block, and mechanical complications
nodes.body: Assess for STEMI complications: \u2022 Cardiogenic shock (5\u201310% of AMI) \u2014 hypotension, cool skin, AMS \u2022 RV involvement (33\u201350% of inferior STEMIs) \u2014 hypotension with clear lungs \u2022 Reperfusion arrhythmias \u2014 PVCs, VT, AIVR, AF, VF \u2022 AV block (7% with thrombolytics) [25] \u2022 Mechanical complications \u2014 VSD, papillary muscle rupture, free wall rupture

nodes.title: Cardiogenic Shock
nodes.body: Cardiogenic shock complicates 5\u201310% of AMI. [26] Immediate management: \u2022 PCI regardless of time from MI onset (Class I) \u2014 basis: the SHOCK trial (n=302) showed a survival benefit for early revascularization vs initial medical stabilization by 6 months, sustained at 6 years [5][23][35] \u2022 Volume resuscitation if no pulmonary edema [5][23] \u2022 Vasopressors to maintain coronary
nodes.recommendation: Emergent PCI regardless of timing. Vasopressors for perfusion. Transfer immediately if not at PCI center. Consider mechanical support.

nodes.title: Right Ventricular Involvement
nodes.summary: RV infarct: STE ≥1 mm V4R — AVOID nitrates/diuretics; volume-dependent, dobutamine if refractory
nodes.body: 33\u201350% of inferior STEMIs involve the right ventricle. [27] Diagnosis \u2014 get right-sided leads: \u2022 STE \u22651 mm in V4R is diagnostic \u2022 Place V1R-V6R as mirror image of standard precordial leads Management \u2014 volume-dependent: \u2022 AVOID nitrates (reduce preload \u2192 hemodynamic collapse) \u2022 AVOID diuretics \u2022 Volume resuscitation with NS boluses (250\u2013500 mL

nodes.title: Reperfusion Arrhythmias
nodes.summary: AIVR is a sign of successful reperfusion — self-limited, do NOT treat with antidysrhythmics
nodes.body: Most common reperfusion arrhythmias: PVCs, VT, AIVR, AF, VF. [24] AIVR (Accelerated Idioventricular Rhythm): \u2022 Regular wide-complex rhythm, rate 50\u2013110 bpm \u2022 Usually a SIGN OF SUCCESSFUL REPERFUSION \u2022 Well-tolerated and self-limited \u2022 Do NOT treat with antidysrhythmics \u2014 may cause hemodynamic collapse \u2022 Resolves when sinus rate exceeds ventricular focus VT/VF: De

nodes.title: Special Populations
nodes.summary: Women: more atypical presentations; elderly: half-dose lytics; cocaine: avoid pure beta-blockers, PCI preferred
nodes.body: Women: \u2022 Less likely to present with central chest pain [28] \u2022 Same risk factors and treatment as men \u2022 CV mortality has remained higher in women since 1980s Elderly (>75 years): \u2022 More atypical presentations (dyspnea, syncope, nausea) \u2022 Higher complication rate, more contraindications to reperfusion \u2022 Age alone is NOT a reason to withhold reperfusion [29] \u2022 Cons

nodes.title: Disposition \u2014 Admit ICU/CCU
nodes.body: All STEMI patients are admitted after reperfusion (PCI or fibrinolysis). In-hospital management (guideline-directed medical therapy \u2014 basis: 2025 ACC/AHA ACS guideline and 2013 ACCF/AHA STEMI guideline): [5][23] \u2022 Continuous cardiac monitoring for reperfusion arrhythmias \u2022 Metoprolol within 24h if no CI (HR, BP permitting) [5][23] \u2022 Atorvastatin 80 mg (start immediately) [5][23
nodes.recommendation: Admit ICU/CCU. Start GDMT: beta-blocker, high-intensity statin, ACEi/ARB. Continue DAPT \u00D712 months. Cardiac rehab referral.

nodes.title: STI Comprehensive Consult
nodes.summary: Syndrome-based empiric treatment — key 2024 updates: doxyPEP, syphilis 3x pregnancy screen, azithromycin no longer for GC
nodes.body: CDC 2024 STI Regimens | Syndromic Rx Picker Syndrome-based approach - treat empirically based on presentation, then narrow based on test results. 2024-2025 Key Updates: - DoxyPEP — CDC clinical guideline (MMWR, June 6 2024) - 200mg doxycycline within 72h post-sex for MSM/TGW with a bacterial STI (syphilis, chlamydia, or gonorrhea) diagnosed in past 12 months; shared decision-making; test at exposu

nodes.title: Presenting Syndrome
nodes.summary: Select presenting syndrome — urethral/cervical, genital ulcer, pelvic/regional, or special population screen
nodes.body: Select the primary clinical syndrome. Multiple syndromes may coexist. Clinical tip: Always test at all sites of exposure (urethral, pharyngeal, rectal) in MSM.

nodes.title: Risk Factor Assessment
nodes.summary: MSM: test all 3 sites; HIV+: same regimens mostly; pregnancy: doxycycline contraindicated; PCN only for syphilis
nodes.body: Higher risk factors requiring expanded testing/treatment: MSM (men who have sex with men): - Test all 3 sites: urethral, pharyngeal, rectal - Higher rates of LGV proctitis, M. genitalium, mpox - Offer doxyPEP if bacterial STI in past 12 months HIV-positive: - Same treatment regimens as HIV-negative (with few exceptions) - Watch for drug interactions with ART - More aggressive suppressive therapy f

nodes.title: Empiric vs Await Testing?
nodes.summary: Empiric treatment if high probability or unreliable follow-up; await results if atypical or treatment failure workup
nodes.body: Expedited empiric treatment is indicated when: - High pretest probability (classic presentation) - Unreliable follow-up - Partner with known infection - Patient preference Consider awaiting results when: - Atypical presentation - Prior treatment failure (need susceptibility testing) - Low pretest probability - Good follow-up assured

nodes.title: STI Testing Overview
nodes.summary: NAAT is gold standard for GC/CT; syphilis: RPR/VDRL for screening + treponemal for confirmation; HIV 4th gen combo
nodes.body: NAAT (Nucleic Acid Amplification Test): - Gold standard for GC/CT detection - Urine, urethral, cervical, rectal, pharyngeal specimens - Results in 1-3 days (some point-of-care in 30 min) Site-specific testing (MSM, based on exposure): - Urethral: urine NAAT or urethral swab - Pharyngeal: throat swab NAAT (lower sensitivity for CT) - Rectal: rectal swab NAAT Syphilis: - Syphilis Staging & Serology

nodes.title: Sexual Assault - Link to DFSA
nodes.summary: Sexual assault: CTX 500mg IM + doxy 100mg BID x 7d + metro 2g PO — see DFSA consult for full protocol
nodes.body: For comprehensive sexual assault workup: DFSA Workup Consult Includes: - Forensic specimen collection timelines - Consent framework - STI prophylaxis (GC, CT, trichomoniasis) - Pregnancy prophylaxis - HIV PEP assessment - Safety and follow-up planning Quick STI prophylaxis for sexual assault: - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 - Doxycycline 100mg BID x 7 days (or azithromycin 1g if pregnant) - Metronidazol

nodes.title: Urethral/Cervical Assessment
nodes.summary: Differentiate male urethritis vs cervicitis vs recurrent/persistent — guides empiric regimen
nodes.body: Urethritis (male): Discharge, dysuria, urethral pruritus Cervicitis: Mucopurulent discharge, cervical friability, intermenstrual bleeding Exam findings: - Urethral discharge (purulent, mucopurulent, or mucoid) - Gram stain: >2 WBC/HPF or positive leukocyte esterase - Cervical mucopus or friability What is the clinical presentation?

nodes.title: Urethritis - Empiric Treatment
nodes.body: Syndromic Rx Picker Empiric treatment covers GC + CT: First-line: - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 (1g if >=150kg) - PLUS Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 7 days 2021 Update: Azithromycin no longer added routinely - ceftriaxone monotherapy for gonorrhea. Alternative (if IM not possible): - Cefixime 800mg PO x1 + Doxycycline 100mg BID x 7d - *Note: Cefixime less reliable for pharyngeal GC* Chlamydia only (GC ru
nodes.recommendation: Treat empirically for both GC and CT. Order NAAT confirmation. Partner therapy within 60 days. Abstain until 7 days after treatment completion.

nodes.title: Cervicitis - Treatment
nodes.body: Same regimen as urethritis: First-line: - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 - PLUS Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 7 days If GC ruled out (CT only): - Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 7 days Pregnancy modification: - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 (same) - PLUS Azithromycin 1g PO x1 (instead of doxycycline) Recurrent cervicitis: - Consider M. genitalium testing - Rule out BV (commonly co-occurs)
nodes.recommendation: Treat empirically. Rule out PID (cervical motion tenderness, uterine/adnexal tenderness). Partner treatment required.

nodes.title: PID Assessment
nodes.summary: PID if cervical motion/uterine/adnexal tenderness present — escalate to PID treatment if any criterion met
nodes.body: Does the patient meet PID criteria? Minimum criteria (any 1 of 3): - Cervical motion tenderness - Uterine tenderness - Adnexal tenderness If any present plus pelvic/lower abdominal pain, diagnose PID and escalate treatment.

nodes.title: Mycoplasma genitalium Workup
nodes.summary: M. genitalium causes 15-25% of NGU — 44-90% macrolide resistant in US; doxy then moxifloxacin if no resistance testing
nodes.body: Consider M. genitalium when: - Persistent/recurrent urethritis or cervicitis - Initial GC/CT treatment failure - NGU with negative GC/CT Key facts: - Causes 15-25% of NGU cases - Macrolide resistance: 44-90% in US - Beta-lactams do NOT work (no cell wall) - NAAT available at reference labs Treatment (resistance testing available): - Macrolide-sensitive: Doxy 100mg BID x 7d, THEN azithromycin 1g da

nodes.title: Pregnancy Modifications
nodes.summary: Pregnancy: doxycycline CI (use azithromycin); syphilis requires PCN only — desensitize if allergic
nodes.body: Pregnancy Drug Safety Safe in pregnancy: - Ceftriaxone (all trimesters) - Azithromycin (all trimesters) - Metronidazole (all trimesters - CDC category B) - Acyclovir/Valacyclovir (safe in pregnancy) Contraindicated in pregnancy: - Doxycycline - use azithromycin 1g x1 instead for CT - Fluoroquinolones (moxifloxacin, ciprofloxacin) - Tinidazole - use metronidazole Syphilis in pregnancy: - Penicillin

nodes.title: HIV+ Modifications
nodes.summary: HIV+: generally same treatment; check ART interactions; more aggressive syphilis follow-up and HSV suppression
nodes.body: Generally same treatment as HIV-negative patients: No changes needed: - Gonorrhea: Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 - Chlamydia: Doxycycline 100mg BID x 7d - Syphilis: Benzathine PCN 2.4 MU IM (same staging/dosing) Considerations: - HSV: May need higher doses or longer duration; suppressive therapy more strongly recommended - Drug interactions: Check ART interactions (especially with fluoroquinolones, azol

nodes.title: Trichomoniasis Treatment
nodes.body: Trichomonas vaginalis - most common curable STI worldwide. Women (7-day regimen preferred - 2021 update): - Metronidazole 500mg PO BID x 7 days Men (single dose adequate): - Metronidazole 2g PO x1 Alternative: - Tinidazole 2g PO x1 (both sexes) - Secnidazole 2g PO x1 Treatment failure: - Metronidazole or tinidazole 2g PO daily x 7 days - Resistance testing available through CDC Pregnancy: - Metron
nodes.recommendation: MUST treat ALL partners - required for cure. EPT recommended. Retest at 3 months.

nodes.title: Bacterial Vaginosis (BV)
nodes.summary: BV: metronidazole 500mg BID x 7d — not strictly STI but frequently co-occurs; 2025 RCT supports partner treatment
nodes.body: Not technically an STI but frequently co-occurs. First-line treatment: - Metronidazole 500mg PO BID x 7 days, OR - Metronidazole gel 0.75% intravaginally daily x 5 days, OR - Clindamycin cream 2% intravaginally at bedtime x 7 days Alternative: - Clindamycin 300mg PO BID x 7 days - Secnidazole 2g PO x1 Partner treatment: - Traditionally NOT recommended - 2025 RCT: Partner treatment reduced recurren

nodes.title: Genital Ulcer Differential
nodes.summary: Ulcer DDx by characteristics: HSV painful/vesicular, syphilis painless/indurated, chancroid painful/purulent, LGV painless
nodes.body: Diagnostic approach based on ulcer characteristics: | Etiology | Pain | Appearance | Other | |----------|------|------------|-------| | HSV | Painful | Vesicles/shallow ulcers, bilateral | May recur | | Syphilis | Painless | Indurated, clean base, single | Firm lymphadenopathy | | Chancroid | Painful | Purulent, ragged edges | Suppurative nodes | | LGV | Painless initially | Small papule | Regiona

nodes.title: HSV Episode Type
nodes.summary: Determine first episode vs recurrent vs frequent recurrences — guides treatment duration and suppressive therapy discussion
nodes.body: Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-1 or HSV-2) First episode: More severe, systemic symptoms common, longer duration Recurrent: Milder, shorter, often with prodrome (tingling, burning) Diagnosis: - PCR/NAAT from lesion (preferred) - Type-specific serology (HSV-1, HSV-2 IgG) - Viral culture (less sensitive than PCR) Is this a first episode or recurrent?

nodes.title: HSV First Episode - Treatment
nodes.body: First episode treatment (7-10 days): | Drug | Dose | Frequency | |------|------|-----------| | Acyclovir | 400mg PO | TID x 7-10d | | Valacyclovir | 1g PO | BID x 7-10d | | Famciclovir | 250mg PO | TID x 7-10d | Extend to 14+ days if healing incomplete. Severe disease (hospitalized): - Acyclovir 5-10 mg/kg IV q8h until improving, then oral to complete course Pregnancy: - Acyclovir and valacyclovir
nodes.recommendation: Start treatment ASAP - most effective within 72h of onset. Counsel on transmission, asymptomatic shedding, and disclosure. Offer suppressive therapy discussion at follow-up.

nodes.title: HSV Recurrent Episode - Treatment
nodes.body: Episodic therapy (start within 24h of onset or during prodrome): | Drug | Dose | Duration | |------|------|----------| | Acyclovir | 400mg PO TID | 5 days | | Acyclovir | 800mg PO BID | 5 days | | Valacyclovir | 500mg PO BID | 3 days | | Valacyclovir | 1g PO daily | 5 days | | Famciclovir | 125mg PO BID | 5 days | Patient-initiated therapy: Prescribe in advance so patient can start at first sympto
nodes.recommendation: Episodic treatment reduces duration by 1-2 days. Discuss suppressive therapy for frequent recurrences. Transmission occurs even without symptoms.

nodes.title: HSV Suppressive Therapy
nodes.body: Indicated for >=6 recurrences/year or to reduce transmission: | Drug | Dose | |------|------| | Acyclovir | 400mg PO BID | | Valacyclovir | 500mg PO daily (1g if >=10 episodes/yr) | | Famciclovir | 250mg PO BID | Benefits: - Reduces recurrences by 70-80% - Reduces transmission to partners by ~50% - Safe for long-term use (years) Reassess annually - many patients have fewer recurrences over time. P
nodes.recommendation: Continue daily suppressive therapy indefinitely. Reassess need annually. Safe for long-term use.

nodes.title: Syphilis Staging
nodes.summary: Syphilis staging determines treatment — primary/secondary/early latent vs late latent vs tertiary vs neuro
nodes.body: Syphilis Staging & Serology | Syphilis Consult Primary: Chancre (painless, indurated ulcer at inoculation site) Secondary: Rash (palms/soles), mucous patches, condyloma lata, systemic symptoms Early Latent: <1 year, asymptomatic, positive serology Late Latent: >1 year or unknown duration, asymptomatic Tertiary: Gummas, cardiovascular syphilis (rare now) Neurosyphilis: Can occur at ANY stage - CSF

nodes.title: Syphilis Treatment
nodes.body: Syphilis Consult - for full workup | Stage | Treatment | |-------|----------| | Primary/Secondary/Early Latent | Benzathine PCN G 2.4 MU IM x1 | | Late Latent/Tertiary | Benzathine PCN G 2.4 MU IM weekly x 3 weeks | | Neurosyphilis | Aqueous PCN G 18-24 MU/day IV x 10-14 days | PCN allergy (non-pregnant): - Early: Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 14 days - Late: Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 28 days - Neur
nodes.recommendation: Follow-up serology at 6 and 12 months (24 months for late latent). Fourfold decline expected by 6-12 months. Evaluate for neurosyphilis if failure to decline.

nodes.title: Chancroid Treatment
nodes.body: Haemophilus ducreyi - rare in US but endemic in some regions. Clinical: Painful ulcer with purulent base, ragged undermined edges. Suppurative inguinal lymphadenopathy ("buboes"). Treatment (any one): - Azithromycin 1g PO x1 - Ceftriaxone 250mg IM x1 - Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO BID x 3 days - Erythromycin base 500mg PO TID x 7 days HIV+: May need longer treatment courses. Monitor closely for healing.
nodes.recommendation: Re-examine in 3-7 days. Ulcers should improve within 7 days. HIV testing required. Partner treatment.

nodes.title: LGV Treatment
nodes.body: Lymphogranuloma venereum - Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3. Presentation: - Small painless papule/ulcer (often unnoticed) - Painful inguinal lymphadenopathy ("groove sign") - MSM: Often presents as severe proctitis Treatment: - Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 21 days Alternative: - Erythromycin base 500mg PO QID x 21 days - Azithromycin 1g PO weekly x 3 weeks (limited data) Note: This is LONG
nodes.recommendation: Extend to 21 days (vs 7 days for non-LGV chlamydia). Consider LGV in any MSM with severe proctitis. Partner treatment within 60 days.

nodes.title: Genital Ulcer - Empiric Treatment
nodes.body: When etiology unclear, treat for HSV + syphilis: HSV coverage: - Valacyclovir 1g PO BID x 7-10 days (or acyclovir 400mg TID) Syphilis coverage: - Benzathine PCN G 2.4 MU IM x1 Add chancroid coverage if: - Endemic area or recent travel - Purulent ulcer with suppurative nodes - Azithromycin 1g PO x1 Testing: - HSV PCR/NAAT from lesion - Syphilis serology (RPR + treponemal) - HIV testing (all patient
nodes.recommendation: Cover both HSV and syphilis empirically when diagnosis unclear. Narrow based on test results.

nodes.title: Pelvic/Regional Syndrome Type
nodes.summary: Select pelvic/regional syndrome — PID, epididymitis, proctitis, or pharyngeal infection
nodes.body: Select the primary syndrome:

nodes.title: PID Severity Assessment
nodes.summary: PID: any 1 of CMT/uterine/adnexal tenderness — hospitalize if pregnant, TOA, severe illness, unable to comply
nodes.body: Minimum diagnostic criteria for PID (sexually active woman with pelvic pain PLUS any 1 of): - Cervical motion tenderness - Uterine tenderness - Adnexal tenderness Hospitalization criteria: - Pregnancy - Tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) - Severe illness (high fever, N/V, temp >38.5C) - Unable to tolerate/comply with outpatient regimen - No improvement after 72h outpatient therapy - Surgical emergency can

nodes.title: PID Outpatient Treatment
nodes.body: Recommended regimen (2021 update - metronidazole now ROUTINE): - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 (1g if >=150kg) - PLUS Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 14 days - PLUS Metronidazole 500mg PO BID x 14 days Alternative: - Cefoxitin 2g IM x1 WITH Probenecid 1g PO x1 - PLUS Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 14 days - PLUS Metronidazole 500mg PO BID x 14 days IUD in place: Do NOT remove. Treat according to guidelines. Reas
nodes.recommendation: Complete full 14-day course. Re-evaluate in 72h - if no improvement, hospitalize. IUD can remain in place. Partner treatment within 60 days.

nodes.title: PID Inpatient Treatment
nodes.body: Parenteral regimen: Recommended: - Ceftriaxone 1g IV q24h - PLUS Doxycycline 100mg PO/IV q12h - PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV/PO q12h Alternative: - Cefotetan 2g IV q12h + Doxycycline 100mg PO/IV q12h, OR - Cefoxitin 2g IV q6h + Doxycycline 100mg PO/IV q12h Transition to oral: After 24-48h clinical improvement, complete 14-day total course with oral doxycycline + metronidazole. Pregnancy: Hospitaliz
nodes.recommendation: IV therapy until 24-48h clinical improvement, then complete 14-day oral course. Imaging for TOA if not improving. Partner treatment.

nodes.title: Epididymitis - Age/Risk Based
nodes.summary: Epididymitis etiology by age: <35 STI (GC/CT), >35 enteric bacteria; MSM needs dual coverage; rule out torsion
nodes.body: Etiology varies by age and risk factors: | Population | Likely Pathogens | |------------|------------------| | Sexually active <35 | GC, CT | | MSM (insertive anal sex) | GC, CT AND enteric bacteria | | Men >35 or recent instrumentation | Enteric bacteria (E. coli, Pseudomonas) | Red flags - consider torsion: - Sudden onset - Absent cremasteric reflex - High-riding testis - Age <25 (torsion peak a

nodes.title: Epididymitis - STI Etiology
nodes.body: GC/CT likely - same regimen as urethritis + extended doxycycline: - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 - PLUS Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 10 days Note: Doxycycline extended to 10 days (vs 7 days for urethritis). Supportive care: - Scrotal elevation - NSAIDs for pain - Ice packs Hospitalization if: - Severe pain suggesting torsion or abscess - Systemic symptoms (fever, unable to take PO) - Diagnostic uncertain
nodes.recommendation: NAAT testing for GC/CT. Partner treatment within 60 days. Supportive care. Reevaluate if no improvement in 48-72h.

nodes.title: Epididymitis - MSM with Insertive Anal
nodes.body: Cover GC/CT AND enteric bacteria: - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 - PLUS Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 10 days - Consider adding Levofloxacin 500mg PO daily x 10 days if enteric organisms suspected Supportive care: - Scrotal elevation, NSAIDs, ice packs Testing: - Urine NAAT for GC/CT - Urine culture (midstream clean catch) for enteric organisms
nodes.recommendation: Broad coverage for both STI and enteric pathogens. NAAT + urine culture. Partner treatment.

nodes.title: Epididymitis - Enteric Organisms
nodes.body: Enteric bacteria (E. coli, Pseudomonas) - NOT STI related: - Levofloxacin 500mg PO daily x 10 days Indications for fluoroquinolone monotherapy: - Age >35 - Recent urologic instrumentation/surgery - Known urologic abnormality - Low STI risk Testing: - Urine culture (midstream clean catch) - UA - Consider prostatic involvement if febrile
nodes.recommendation: Urine culture to guide therapy. If STI not ruled out, add ceftriaxone and NAAT.

nodes.title: Proctitis Treatment (MSM Focus)
nodes.body: Etiology in MSM: GC, CT (including LGV), HSV, syphilis. Differential includes mpox - consider if skin lesions present. Empiric treatment: - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 - PLUS Doxycycline 100mg PO BID x 7 days (extend to 21 days if LGV suspected) HSV proctitis: - Valacyclovir 1g PO BID x 7-10 days, OR - Acyclovir 400mg PO TID x 7-10 days Testing: - Rectal NAAT for GC/CT - LGV PCR if available - HSV NAA
nodes.recommendation: Empiric treatment. Extend doxycycline to 21 days if LGV confirmed or strongly suspected. Screen for HIV, syphilis. Consider mpox in differential.

nodes.title: Pharyngeal GC/CT
nodes.body: Often asymptomatic. Test if oral exposure history. Key points: - More difficult to eradicate than urogenital/rectal - NO reliable alternative to ceftriaxone for pharyngeal GC - Test of cure REQUIRED for all pharyngeal gonorrhea Treatment: - Ceftriaxone 500mg IM x1 (ONLY recommended regimen) - If chlamydia not excluded: add Doxycycline 100mg BID x 7d Test of cure: - Required for ALL pharyngeal gono
nodes.recommendation: Test of cure REQUIRED 7-14 days post-treatment. No reliable oral alternative. Report treatment failures.

nodes.title: Special Population
nodes.summary: Select special population for targeted screening and treatment guidance
nodes.body: Select the special population for targeted guidance:

nodes.title: STI Screening in Pregnancy
nodes.summary: ACOG 2024: syphilis screening 3x (1st visit, 28-32w, delivery); HSV suppression from 36 weeks if history
nodes.body: Pregnancy Drug Safety Routine screening at first prenatal visit: - HIV - Syphilis (RPR/VDRL + treponemal) - Hepatitis B (HBsAg) - Chlamydia - Gonorrhea (if <25 or high-risk) Syphilis screening (ACOG 2024 - 3x screening now standard): - 1st prenatal visit - 28-32 weeks gestation - At delivery Third trimester rescreen (high-risk): - Age <25 - Multiple partners - New partner - Partner with STI - Prio

nodes.title: MSM-Specific Considerations
nodes.summary: MSM: test all 3 sites; doxyPEP 200mg within 72h post-sex reduces syphilis 73-87%, CT 70-88%, GC ~50%
nodes.body: DoxyPEP Eligibility Testing - all 3 anatomic sites: - Urethral: urine NAAT or swab - Pharyngeal: throat swab NAAT - Rectal: rectal swab NAAT Higher prevalence conditions: - LGV proctitis (C. trachomatis L1-L3) - M. genitalium - Hepatitis A (recommend vaccination) Mpox differential: - Consider in MSM with genital/perianal lesions - Can present as proctitis - Does NOT rule out concurrent STI - test

nodes.title: Adolescent STI Care
nodes.summary: Minor consent in most states; screen for trafficking; same regimens as adults; vaccination catch-up (HPV, HepA/B)
nodes.body: Confidentiality: - In most states, minors can consent to STI diagnosis and treatment without parental consent - Check your state-specific laws - Maintain confidentiality to promote health-seeking behavior Consent considerations: - Minor consent laws vary by state - Generally, minors can consent to: STI testing/treatment, contraception, prenatal care - Document capacity and understanding Special co

nodes.title: DoxyPEP Guidance
nodes.body: DoxyPEP Eligibility Tool CDC Guidelines (June 2024): Who should be offered doxyPEP: - Gay/bisexual men (MSM) with bacterial STI in past 12 months - Transgender women with bacterial STI in past 12 months - Can discuss with MSM/TGW without recent STI who engage in high-risk activities Dosing: - Doxycycline 200mg PO as soon as possible, within 72 hours after oral, vaginal, or anal sex - Maximum: 200m
nodes.recommendation: Offer to eligible MSM/TGW. Does not replace condoms or HIV PrEP. Regular STI screening required.

nodes.title: Mpox in STI Differential
nodes.summary: Consider mpox in MSM with genital/perianal lesions — 41% had STI in prior year; TEST FOR BOTH
nodes.body: Consider mpox when: - MSM or transgender women with new skin lesions - Anyone with genital/perianal ulcers - High local mpox incidence Clinical features: - Skin lesions (vesicles, pustules, ulcers) - Can mimic HSV, syphilis, chancroid - May present as proctitis - Systemic symptoms (fever, lymphadenopathy) Key point: Mpox does NOT rule out STI - 41% of mpox patients reported STI in prior year - 38%

nodes.title: Partner Management
nodes.summary: Partners within 60 days evaluated + treated; EPT legal in 47 states — CT/doxy, GC/cefixime, trich/metro
nodes.body: EPT Generator Partner notification: - Sex partners within 60 days should be evaluated and treated - For syphilis, extend lookback period based on staging Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT): - Patient provides medication/prescription to partner - Legal in 47 states + DC (not allowed: Kansas, South Dakota) - Most effective for chlamydia EPT regimens: | Infection | EPT Regimen | |-----------|-----------

nodes.title: Test of Cure Indications
nodes.summary: TOC required for pharyngeal GC (7-14d), pregnancy (3-4w), treatment failure; retest ALL GC/CT at 3 months
nodes.body: Test of cure (TOC) REQUIRED: - Pharyngeal gonorrhea - all cases (7-14 days post-treatment) - Pregnancy - GC and CT (3-4 weeks post-treatment) - Treatment failure or persistent symptoms - HIV+ with syphilis - RPR titers TOC NOT routinely required: - Uncomplicated urogenital GC/CT in non-pregnant adults Reinfection screening (NOT test of cure): - Retest ALL patients with GC/CT at 3 months - Reinfect

nodes.title: Reporting Requirements
nodes.summary: Nationally notifiable: syphilis, GC, CT, chancroid, HIV — report suspected GC treatment failures to CDC/health dept
nodes.body: Nationally notifiable STIs (report to state/local health department): - Syphilis (all stages) - Gonorrhea - Chlamydia - Chancroid - HIV State-specific reporting: - Requirements vary by state - Check local health department guidelines - Most labs auto-report positive results Contact tracing: - Health department may assist with partner notification - Especially important for syphilis clusters Antimi

nodes.title: Follow-Up Summary
nodes.body: Standard follow-up schedule: All STIs: - Abstain from sex until treatment complete and symptoms resolved - Partner treatment within 60 days - Retest for reinfection at 3 months Syphilis: - RPR/VDRL titers at 6 and 12 months (24 months for late latent) - Fourfold decline expected by 6-12 months Pharyngeal GC: - Test of cure at 7-14 days (REQUIRED) Pregnancy: - Test of cure for GC/CT at 3-4 weeks -
nodes.recommendation: Ensure patient understands follow-up schedule. Provide written instructions. Partner treatment critical to prevent reinfection.

nodes.title: Ischemic Stroke Assumed
nodes.summary: Establish last-known-well time, get NIHSS, fingerstick glucose — CT to rule out hemorrhage before thrombolytics
nodes.body: Ischemic Stroke Steps Summary — time-critical reperfusion pathway. We do not yet know if this is ischemic or hemorrhagic. If ICH (intracerebral hemorrhage) is highly suspicious, rule out with CT head non-contrast before proceeding. Establish last known well time. Immediate actions: \u2022 Fingerstick glucose (only pre-tPA lab required) \u2022 Obtain NIHSS (NIH Stroke Scale) score \u2022 Use Syndro

nodes.title: Deficit Severity
nodes.summary: Classify deficit severity by NIHSS — disabling (>=6) routes to reperfusion, minor to DAPT pathway
nodes.body: Is a disabling deficit present? Use the NIHSS calculator below to score the deficit. NIHSS >5 = disabling. Use the Syndrome Calculator when the pattern matters more than the number: aphasia, neglect, field cut, posterior circulation signs, retinal ischemia, or lacunar-appearing deficits. Disabling = deficit that would impair activities of daily living (e.g., limb weakness, aphasia, neglect, visual

nodes.title: Time from Last Known Well
nodes.summary: Time from last known well determines treatment window — 0-4.5h IVT, 4.5-9h extended, 9-24h EVT only
nodes.body: How long since the patient was last known well (not time of symptom discovery)? For wake-up strokes or unknown onset: treat as time from when last seen normal. MRI DWI-FLAIR mismatch may help identify candidates within 4.5h window.

nodes.title: IVT Eligibility
nodes.summary: Check contraindications and BP <185/110 before IVT — labetalol or nicardipine to control BP
nodes.body: Review Thrombolysis Contraindications before proceeding. BP requirement: Must be <185/110 mmHg \u2022 Labetalol 10\u201320 mg IV bolus (first-line) \u2022 Nicardipine 5 mg/hr IV infusion (second-line) If BP cannot be controlled to <185/110, thrombolysis is contraindicated. Labs: Do NOT wait for coags unless patient is on anticoagulants or has known coagulopathy. Fingerstick glucose is the only req

nodes.title: Administer Thrombolysis
nodes.summary: Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg preferred single bolus — BP <180/105 x24h, no antithrombotics x24h, neuro checks q15min
nodes.body: Preferred: Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg IV bolus (max 25 mg) \u2014 single dose over 5 seconds. Alternative: Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg IV (max 90 mg) \u2014 10% bolus over 1 min, remainder over 60 min. Tenecteplase is preferred per current guidelines due to equivalent efficacy, single bolus administration, and simpler dosing. IVT Consent Infographic | Patient Consent Info Post-thrombolysis orders: \u2022 BP

nodes.title: Large Vessel Occlusion?
nodes.summary: Review CTA for LVO (ICA, M1, basilar) — LVO present activates neurointerventional team for EVT
nodes.body: Review CTA results. Is a large vessel occlusion (LVO) present? LVO targets for EVT: \u2022 ICA (internal carotid artery) \u2022 M1 segment of MCA (middle cerebral artery) \u2022 M2 (proximal) MCA \u2014 may be considered \u2022 Basilar artery

nodes.title: IVT Contraindicated
nodes.summary: IVT contraindicated but EVT still possible — get CTA for LVO regardless of thrombolysis eligibility
nodes.body: IVT is contraindicated. However, EVT is NOT contraindicated by thrombolysis exclusion criteria \u2014 patients with contraindications to IVT may still qualify for mechanical thrombectomy. Obtain CTA if not already done.

nodes.title: Extended IVT Window (4.5\u20139h)
nodes.summary: Extended 4.5-9h window requires perfusion imaging — DWI-FLAIR mismatch or CT perfusion with salvageable tissue (core <70mL)
nodes.body: Perfusion imaging is required to determine eligibility. See Stroke Imaging Guide for details on CT perfusion and MRI protocols. EXTEND trial criteria (alteplase 4.5\u20139h): \u2022 DWI-FLAIR (diffusion-weighted imaging / fluid-attenuated inversion recovery) mismatch on MRI (DWI+, FLAIR\u2212 suggests <4.5h) \u2022 OR CT perfusion showing salvageable tissue \u2022 Ischemic core <70 mL \u2022 Penum

nodes.title: EVT Eligibility (6\u201324h)
nodes.summary: EVT 6-24h window: DAWN/DEFUSE-3 criteria for anterior (NIHSS >=6, ICA/M1, small core), ATTENTION for basilar up to 24h
nodes.body: Anterior circulation (DAWN/DEFUSE-3 criteria): \u2022 NIHSS \u22656 \u2022 ICA or M1 occlusion on CTA \u2022 Small ischemic core on CT perfusion (<70 mL at 6\u201316h; <21 mL at 16\u201324h) \u2022 Large penumbra with mismatch ratio >1.8 Large-core (SELECT2/ANGEL-ASPECT): EVT benefit extends to large ischemic cores (ASPECTS 3\u20135 or core \u226550 mL) in selected patients up to 24h. Posterior ci

nodes.title: Activate Neurointerventional Team
nodes.body: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) indicated. Goal: arterial puncture within 60 minutes of arrival. \u2022 Bridging IVT: If within 4.5h and no IVT contraindications, administer Tenecteplase or Alteplase before/during transfer to angio suite \u2014 do NOT delay EVT for thrombolytic infusion to complete \u2022 NPO for sedation/general anesthesia \u2022 Continuous BP monitoring (arterial line) \u2022 Go
nodes.recommendation: Activate neurointerventional team immediately. Administer bridging IVT if within window and no contraindications. Target door-to-puncture <60 min.

nodes.title: Beyond Reperfusion Window
nodes.summary: Beyond 24h — no IVT or EVT, focus on antiplatelet initiation, stroke etiology workup, secondary prevention, and admission
nodes.body: >24 hours from last known well. Not a candidate for IVT or EVT. Focus on: \u2022 Antiplatelet initiation \u2022 Stroke etiology workup \u2022 Secondary prevention \u2022 Admission for neuro monitoring and rehab evaluation

nodes.title: Minor Stroke Workup
nodes.summary: Minor stroke (NIHSS 0-5): MRI preferred, ABCD2 score for risk — high risk gets DAPT, low risk gets single antiplatelet
nodes.body: NIHSS 0\u20135, nondisabling deficit. MRI with DWI is preferred (identifies small infarcts missed on CT). ABCD2 Score (TIA risk stratification): Age \u226560 (+1), BP \u2265140/90 (+1), Clinical features: unilateral weakness (+2) or speech impairment (+1), Duration \u226560min (+2) or 10\u201359min (+1), Diabetes (+1). Infarct on imaging or ABCD2 \u22654 = higher risk of recurrent stroke.

nodes.title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy (DAPT)
nodes.body: Loading (Day 1): \u2022 Aspirin 325 mg + Clopidogrel 300 mg Maintenance: \u2022 Aspirin 81 mg + Clopidogrel 75 mg daily \u00D7 21 days \u2022 Then single antiplatelet (either agent) Alternative (CYP2C19 poor metabolizer): \u2022 Ticagrelor 180 mg load + Aspirin 300 mg, then Ticagrelor 90 mg BID \u00D7 90 days total + Aspirin 81 mg \u00D7 21 days only \u2014 aspirin discontinued after day 21, ticag
nodes.recommendation: Start DAPT immediately. Limit duration to 21 days. Add high-intensity statin. Complete stroke etiology workup.

nodes.title: Single Antiplatelet Therapy
nodes.body: Aspirin 160\u2013325 mg within 24\u201348h of symptom onset, then 81 mg daily. Complete stroke workup: \u2022 Telemetry / cardiac monitoring \u00D7 24h minimum \u2022 Echocardiogram (TTE (transthoracic); TEE (transesophageal) if suspected PFO (patent foramen ovale) or valve pathology) \u2022 Lipid panel \u2192 high-intensity statin \u2022 HbA1c \u2022 Extended cardiac monitoring if etiology unclea
nodes.recommendation: Start aspirin. Complete stroke etiology workup. Initiate statin therapy.

nodes.title: Post-Thrombolysis Management
nodes.summary: Post-tPA: BP <180/105 x24h, neuro checks q15min, no antithrombotics x24h, repeat NCCT at 24h before starting antiplatelets
nodes.body: BP management \u00D7 24h: \u2022 Target <180/105 mmHg \u2022 Labetalol bolus \u00B1 infusion (first-line) \u2022 Nicardipine infusion (alternative) \u2022 Clevidipine (if faster titration needed) Neuro checks protocol: \u2022 Every 15 min \u00D7 2h \u2022 Then every 30 min \u00D7 6h \u2022 Then hourly \u00D7 16h \u2022 Any decline \u2192 emergent NCCT Antithrombotics: \u2022 NO aspirin, heparin, o

nodes.title: Antiplatelet Initiation
nodes.summary: Aspirin 160-325mg within 24-48h if no IVT, or after 24h NCCT if post-IVT — consider DAPT for high-risk minor stroke
nodes.body: If no IVT given: \u2022 Aspirin 160\u2013325 mg within 24\u201348h of onset If post-IVT: \u2022 Wait 24h, obtain NCCT first \u2022 If no hemorrhage: start aspirin 81\u2013325 mg Consider DAPT (aspirin + clopidogrel) for minor stroke with high-risk features (see minor stroke pathway).

nodes.title: Stroke Etiology Workup
nodes.summary: Determine stroke mechanism: telemetry >=24h, echo, carotid/vertebral imaging, lipids, HbA1c — guides secondary prevention
nodes.body: Determine stroke mechanism to guide secondary prevention. Standard workup: \u2022 Continuous telemetry (\u226524h, ideally \u226548h) \u2022 Echocardiogram (TTE \u00B1 TEE) \u2022 Carotid/vertebral imaging (CTA or duplex) \u2022 Lipid panel, HbA1c, BMP \u2022 Hypercoagulability panel if age <60 and cryptogenic

nodes.title: Cardioembolic Stroke \u2014 Anticoagulation
nodes.body: DOAC (direct oral anticoagulant) preferred over warfarin (unless mechanical valve or moderate-severe mitral stenosis). Recommended agents: \u2022 Apixaban 5 mg BID (preferred for stroke prevention, ARISTOTLE trial) \u2022 Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily with food Timing of anticoagulation initiation (based on stroke severity): \u2022 TIA: 1\u20133 days \u2022 Minor stroke (NIHSS <8): 4\u20137 days \u2022
nodes.recommendation: Start DOAC based on stroke severity timing. Do not bridge with heparin. Ensure rate/rhythm control of AF.

nodes.title: Large Artery Atherosclerotic Stroke
nodes.body: Antiplatelet: \u2022 Aspirin 325 mg daily (or DAPT \u00D7 21\u201390 days for intracranial stenosis) Statin: \u2022 High-intensity statin (Atorvastatin 40\u201380 mg or rosuvastatin 20\u201340 mg) \u2022 Target LDL <70 mg/dL Carotid stenosis management: \u2022 Symptomatic 70\u201399% stenosis: CEA (carotid endarterectomy) within 2 weeks (Class I) \u2022 Symptomatic 50\u201369%: CEA is reasonable (
nodes.recommendation: Aspirin + high-intensity statin. Refer for CEA within 2 weeks if symptomatic carotid stenosis 70\u201399%. DAPT \u00D7 90d for intracranial stenosis.

nodes.title: Secondary Prevention \u2014 Other/Cryptogenic
nodes.body: Antiplatelet: \u2022 Aspirin 81 mg daily Statin: \u2022 High-intensity statin regardless of baseline LDL Blood pressure: \u2022 Target <130/80 mmHg (after acute phase) \u2022 Initiate antihypertensive before discharge if stable Extended cardiac monitoring: \u2022 If cryptogenic: 14\u201330 day ambulatory cardiac monitor \u2022 Detects paroxysmal AF in ~12% of cryptogenic strokes \u2022 If AF detec
nodes.recommendation: Aspirin 81 mg + high-intensity statin. BP target <130/80. Extended cardiac monitoring for cryptogenic. PFO closure if criteria met.

nodes.title: Suicidal Patient
nodes.summary: 50% of suicide decedents seen in healthcare within 30 days. Universal screening required.
nodes.body: Steps Summary Why screening matters: • 50% of suicide decedents seen in healthcare within 30 days of death • 80% deny suicidal ideation at last visit • Universal screening detects at-risk patients Joint Commission NPSG 15.01.01: Screen ALL patients using validated tool.

nodes.title: Immediate Safety
nodes.summary: 1:1 observation, remove ligatures/sharps/meds, patient in gown, never leave alone.
nodes.body: Environmental safety — do FIRST: ✓ 1:1 constant visual observation ✓ Remove from room: • Ligatures (clothing, sheets, cords) • Sharps (needles, razors, glass) • Medications (all — including patient's own) • Plastic bags ✓ Secure windows and exits ✓ Patient in gown (remove belt, shoelaces) ✓ Metal detector wand if available Do NOT leave patient alone — even for tests/imaging.

nodes.title: Screening Tool
nodes.summary: ASQ = quick screening. C-SSRS = detailed assessment.
nodes.body: Which screening tool to use? Both are Joint Commission-validated.

nodes.title: ASQ Screening
nodes.summary: ASQ: 4 questions. Any YES = positive screen, needs full C-SSRS assessment.
nodes.body: Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ): 1. In the past few weeks, have you wished you were dead? 2. In the past few weeks, have you felt that you or your family would be better off if you were dead? 3. In the past week, have you been having thoughts about killing yourself? 4. Have you ever tried to kill yourself? If YES to any: → Positive screen If ALL NO: Ask acuity question: "Are you having thoug

nodes.title: C-SSRS Assessment
nodes.summary: C-SSRS: 5 levels of ideation severity. Stop at first NO.
nodes.body: Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale Assess in order — stop at first NO: 1. Wish to be dead? (passive ideation) 2. Non-specific active thoughts? ("wanting to end my life") 3. Active ideation with method? (thinking about how) 4. Active ideation with intent? (intending to act) 5. Active ideation with plan? (specific plan formed) Also assess: • Preparatory behaviors (giving away possessions, writin

nodes.title: C-SSRS Result
nodes.summary: C-SSRS level determines risk category and disposition pathway.
nodes.body: What is the highest level endorsed?

nodes.title: Low Acute Risk
nodes.summary: Low risk — provide crisis resources, schedule follow-up, brief counseling.
nodes.body: Low risk does NOT mean no risk. Protective factors: • Strong social support • Engaged in treatment • Problem-solving skills • Reasons for living • Children at home • Religious/spiritual beliefs Still required: • Brief counseling on warning signs • Crisis resources (988 Lifeline) • Follow-up appointment scheduled

nodes.title: Moderate Risk
nodes.summary: Moderate risk — assess modifying factors (prior attempts, means access, support).
nodes.body: Passive ideation or non-specific active thoughts Assess modifying factors: Elevating risk: • Recent loss (relationship, job, health) • Social isolation • Substance use • Prior attempts (strongest predictor) • Family history of suicide • Access to lethal means • Hopelessness • Impulsivity Protective factors: • Engaged in treatment • Future orientation • Social support • Reasons for living

nodes.title: High Risk
nodes.summary: High risk — psych consult, means restriction, safety plan, no discharge without eval.
nodes.body: Active ideation WITH method This patient has thought about HOW. Required: • Continue 1:1 observation • Psychiatric consultation • Means restriction counseling • Safety planning • Consider voluntary or involuntary admission Do NOT discharge without: • Psychiatry evaluation • Documented safety plan • Means restriction addressed • Follow-up within 24-72 hours

nodes.title: Imminent Risk
nodes.summary: Imminent risk — STAT psych, 1:1, no discharge. Voluntary or involuntary admission.
nodes.body: Intent, plan, or recent attempt ⚠️ HIGHEST RISK — requires admission Immediate actions: • Continuous 1:1 observation • STAT psychiatry consult • Search for concealed means (wand, pockets) • Medical stabilization if post-attempt • Notify family (if appropriate) Disposition: • Voluntary psychiatric admission preferred • Involuntary hold if refuses AND meets criteria • Do NOT discharge

nodes.title: Means Restriction Counseling
nodes.summary: Means restriction saves lives. Firearms = ~90% case fatality. Use CALM approach.
